*Word for word:* tatah — then; vivahe nirvritte — when the wedding was complete; kritva — having held; cha — and; su-maha-utsavam — a very great festival; ajagama — came; nijam — to His own; geham — house; sa-bharyah — with His wife; jagatam — of the worlds; guruh — the Teacher.

**32.** When the wedding was complete and a great festival had been held, the Teacher of the worlds returned with His wife to His own house.

### Verse 33

दृष्ट्वा तु तं क्षितिसुरैरभिनन्द्यमानं
वध्वा समं सपदि गेहमुपागतं सा।
गेहप्रवेशनविधिं मुदिता चकार
साध्वीभिर्बन्धुरमुखी जननी मुरारेः॥३३॥

*dṛṣṭvā tu taṁ kṣitisurairabhinandyamānaṁ*
*vadhvā samaṁ sapadi gehamupāgataṁ sā|*

*Word for word:* drishtva — seeing; tu — and; tam — Him; kshiti-suraih — by the gods on earth (brahmanas); abhinandyamanam — being greeted; vadhva samam — together with the bride; sapadi — soon; geham — to the house; upagatam — come; sa — she; geha-praveshana-vidhim — the rite of entering the house; mudita — joyful; chakara — performed; sadhvibhih — with virtuous women; bandhura-mukhi — lovely-faced; janani — the mother; murareh — of Murari (Krishna).

**33.** Seeing Him soon arrive home with the bride, greeted by the gods on earth[^114-7], the lovely-faced mother of Murari[^114-8] joyfully performed, with the virtuous women, the rite of entering the house.

*Thus ends the fourteenth sarga, "The Marriage of Sri Vishnupriya" (Shri-vishnupriya-vivaha), of the first prakrama of the great poem "Sri Krishna-chaitanya-charitamrita."*

[^114-1]: The lagna is the zodiacal sign rising at the moment of the rite; a nakshatra is a lunar asterism. Their favourable conjunction with the moon determines the time of the wedding.
[^114-2]: Betel (tambula): betel leaves with areca nut and spices, offered to guests.
[^114-3]: The nandimukha are forefathers honoured with a special rite (nandimukha shraddha) before a wedding and other joyful occasions.
[^114-4]: Literally, "with a gracious face."
[^114-5]: Nirmanchhana: the rite of waving lamps and other auspicious things around the bridegroom to ward off the evil eye.
[^114-6]: Rohini is the nakshatra who is the favourite consort of the moon-god.
[^114-7]: The gods on earth are the brahmanas.
[^114-8]: Murari ("Enemy of Mura") is Krishna; here, Gauranga.

## Prakrama 1, Sarga 15. The Meeting with Srimad Ishvara Puri

*The Lord lives at home, teaching and gladdening His mother and wife; the journey to Gaya for His father's rite; a fever cured by the water from brahmanas' feet; the meeting with Ishvara Puri and initiation into the mantra*

### Verse 1

ततः पुरस्थैरभिनन्दितो हरि-
र्वसन्गृहे ब्राह्मणवैद्यसज्जनान्।
अपाठयल्लौकिकसत्क्रियाविधिं
चकार कारुण्यविधानमद्भुतम्॥१॥

*tataḥ purasthairabhinandito hari-*
*rvasangṛhe brāhmaṇavaidyasajjanān|*
*apāṭhayallaukikasatkriyāvidhiṁ*
*cakāra kāruṇyavidhānamadbhutam||1||*

*Word for word:* tatah — then; pura-sthaih — by the townspeople; abhinanditah — greeted; harih — Hari; vasan — living; grihe — at home; brahmana-vaidya-sajjanan — brahmanas, vaidyas and good people; apathayat — taught; laukika-sat-kriya-vidhim — the rules of good worldly rites; chakara — observed; karunya-vidhanam — a work of mercy; adbhutam — wondrous.

**1.** Then Hari, greeted by the townspeople, lived at home: He taught brahmanas, vaidyas[^115-1] and good people and observed the rules of good worldly rites — and this was a wondrous work of His mercy.

### Verse 2

वाचस्पतेर्वाग्मितया जहार
काव्यस्य काव्येन विधोः श्रियं सः।
कान्त्या स्वयं भूमिगते सुरेशे
न्यस्तां पुनस्तां हरये ददुः किम्॥२॥

*vācaspatervāgmitayā jahāra*
*kāvyasya kāvyena vidhoḥ śriyaṁ saḥ|*
*kāntyā svayaṁ bhūmigate sureśe*
*nyastāṁ punastāṁ haraye daduḥ kim||2||*

*Word for word:* vachaspateh — of Vachaspati (Brihaspati); vagmitaya — by eloquence; jahara — took away; kavyasya — of Kavya (Shukra); kavyena — by poetry; vidhoh — of the moon; shriyam — the splendour; sah — He; kantya — by radiance; svayam — Himself; bhumi-gate — having come to earth; sura-ishe — the Lord of the gods; nyastam — entrusted; punah — back; tam — it; haraye — to Hari; daduh — they gave; kim — did (they not)?

**2.** By His eloquence He took away the glory of Vachaspati, by His poetry that of Kavya, by His radiance the splendour of the moon[^115-2]. When the Lord of the gods Himself had come to earth, did they not give back to Hari what had been entrusted to them?

### Verse 3

सोऽध्यापयद्विप्रमहत्तमांस्तान्
ये पूर्वजन्मार्जितपुण्यराशयः।
ब्रूमः कथं भाग्यवतां महद्गुणं
येषां स्वयं लोकगुरुर्गुरुर्भवेत्॥३॥

*so'dhyāpayadvipramahattamāṁstān*
*ye pūrvajanmārjitapuṇyarāśayaḥ|*
*brūmaḥ kathaṁ bhāgyavatāṁ mahadguṇaṁ*
*yeṣāṁ svayaṁ lokagururgururbhavet||3||*

*Word for word:* sah — He; adhyapayat — taught; vipra-mahattaman — the greatest of brahmanas; tan — those; ye — who; purva-janma-arjita-punya-rashayah — had amassed heaps of merit in former births; brumah — shall we tell; katham — how; bhagyavatam — of the fortunate ones; mahat-gunam — the great merit; yesham — whose; svayam — Himself; loka-guruh — the Teacher of the world; guruh — teacher; bhavet — became.

**3.** He taught the greatest of brahmanas — those who in former births had amassed heaps of merit. How can we describe the great merit of those fortunate ones, whose teacher the Teacher of the world Himself became?

### Verse 4

सौन्दर्यमाधुर्यविलासविभ्रमै-
रराज राजद्वरहेमगौरः।
विष्णुप्रियालालितपादपङ्कजो
रसेन पूर्णो रसिकेन्द्रमौलिः॥४॥

*saundaryamādhuryavilāsavibhramai-*
*rarāja rājadvarahemagauraḥ|*
*viṣṇupriyālālitapādapaṅkajo*
*rasena pūrṇo rasikendramauliḥ||4||*

*Word for word:* saundarya-madhurya-vilasa-vibhramaih — with beauty, sweetness, playfulness and charm; raraja — shone; rajat-vara-hema-gaurah — golden like gleaming pure gold; vishnupriya-lalita-pada-pankajah — whose lotus feet were caressed by Vishnupriya; rasena — with rasa; purnah — full; rasika-indra-maulih — the crown of the kings of rasikas.

**4.** Gleaming like pure gold, He shone with beauty, sweetness, playfulness and charm. Vishnupriya caressed His lotus feet; full of rasa, He was the crown of the kings of rasikas[^115-3].

### Verse 5

विद्याविलासेन विलोलबाहु-
र्गच्छन्पथि शिष्यसमाकुलो हरिः।
आगत्य गेहे निजमातुरन्तिके
तस्याः सुखं नित्यमधात्प्रियासमम्॥५॥

*vidyāvilāsena vilolabāhu-*
*rgacchanpathi śiṣyasamākulo hariḥ|*
*āgatya gehe nijamāturantike*
*tasyāḥ sukhaṁ nityamadhātpriyāsamam||5||*

*Word for word:* vidya-vilasena — in the play of learning; vilola-bahuh — swinging His arms; gachchhan — walking; pathi — on the road; shishya-samakulah — thronged by students; harih — Hari; agatya — coming; gehe — home; nija-matuh — of His mother; antike — into the presence; tasyah — to her; sukham — joy; nityam — always; adhat — gave; priya-samam — equally with His beloved.

**5.** Rapt in the play of learning, Hari walked along the road swinging His arms, thronged by His students; and coming home to His mother, He always gave her joy equally with His beloved wife.

### Verse 6

ततः स लोकाननुशिक्षयन्मन-
श्चकार कर्तुं पितृकार्यमच्युतः।
श्राद्धं स कृत्वा विधिवद्विधानवि-
द्गयां प्रतस्थे क्षितिदेवतान्वितः॥६॥

*tataḥ sa lokānanuśikṣayanmana-*
*ścakāra kartuṁ pitṛkāryamacyutaḥ|*
*śrāddhaṁ sa kṛtvā vidhivadvidhānavi-*
*dgayāṁ pratasthe kṣitidevatānvitaḥ||6||*

*Word for word:* tatah — then; sah — He; lokan — people; anushikshayan — teaching; manah chakara — resolved; kartum — to perform; pitri-karyam — the rite for His father; achyutah — Achyuta; shraddham — the shraddha; sah — He; kritva — performing; vidhivat — duly; vidhana-vit — knower of the injunctions; gayam — for Gaya; pratasthe — set out; kshiti-devata-anvitah — accompanied by the gods on earth (brahmanas).

**6.** Then Achyuta, teaching people, resolved to perform the rite for His father. Knower of the injunctions, He duly performed the shraddha and set out for Gaya with the gods on earth[^115-4].

### Verse 7

गच्छन्पथि प्राकृतचेष्टया हस-
न्नर्मोक्तिभिः कौतुकमावहन्सताम्।
रेमे कुरङ्गावलिराजितासु
स्थलीषु पश्यन्मृगकौतुकानि॥७॥

*gacchanpathi prākṛtaceṣṭayā hasa-*
*nnarmoktibhiḥ kautukamāvahansatām|*
*reme kuraṅgāvalirājitāsu*
*sthalīṣu paśyanmṛgakautukāni||7||*

*Word for word:* gachchhan — going; pathi — along the road; prakrita-cheshtaya — with the manners of an ordinary man; hasan — laughing; narma-uktibhih — with jests; kautukam — merriment; avahan — bringing; satam — to the good; reme — He delighted; kuranga-avali-rajitasu — graced by herds of antelope; sthalishu — on the plains; pashyan — watching; mriga-kautukani — the frolics of the animals.

**7.** Going along the road, He behaved like an ordinary man: He laughed and amused the good with His jests, and on the plains graced by herds of antelope He delighted in watching the frolics of the animals.

### Verse 8

स्नात्वा स चोरान्धयके नदे मुदा
कृत्वाह्निकं देवपितॄन्यथाविधि।
सन्तर्पयित्वा सहसान्वितः प्रियै-
र्मन्दारमारुह्य ददर्श देवताः॥८॥

*snātvā sa corāndhayake nade mudā*
*kṛtvāhnikaṁ devapitṝnyathāvidhi|*
*santarpayitvā sahasānvitaḥ priyai-*
*rmandāramāruhya dadarśa devatāḥ||8||*

*Word for word:* snatva — bathing; sah — He; chorandhayake nade — in the river Chorandhayaka; muda — joyfully; kritva — performing; ahnikam — the daily rites; deva-pitrin — the gods and forefathers; yatha-vidhi — according to the rules; santarpayitva — satisfying (with libations); sahasa — then at once; anvitah priyaih — with His dear companions; mandaram — Mandara; aruhya — climbing; dadarsha — saw; devatah — the deities.

**8.** Having joyfully bathed in the river Chorandhayaka and performed His daily rites according to the rules, He satisfied the gods and forefathers with libations, and then, with His dear companions, climbed Mount Mandara and saw the deities there[^115-5].

### Verse 9

ततोऽवतीर्यावजगाम सत्वरं
धराधराधो भवनं द्विजस्य सः।
मनुष्यशिक्षामनुदर्शयन्प्रभु-
र्ज्वरेण सन्तप्ततनुर्बभूव॥९॥

*tato'vatīryāvajagāma satvaraṁ*
*dharādharādho bhavanaṁ dvijasya saḥ|*
*manuṣyaśikṣāmanudarśayanprabhu-*
*rjvareṇa santaptatanurbabhūva||9||*

*Word for word:* tatah — then; avatirya — descending; avajagama — went down; satvaram — quickly; dharadhara-adhah — at the foot of the mountain; bhavanam — to the house; dvijasya — of a brahmana; sah — He; manushya-shiksham — a lesson for men; anudarshayan — showing; prabhuh — Prabhu; jvarena — with fever; santapta-tanuh — His body burning; babhuva — became.

**9.** Then Prabhu quickly came down to the house of a brahmana at the foot of the mountain; and, giving a lesson to people, He fell ill with a burning fever.

### Verse 10

बभूव मे वर्त्मनि दैवयोगा-
च्छरीरवैवश्यमतः कथं स्यात्।
गयासु मे पैतृककर्मविघ्नः
श्रेयस्यभूदित्यतिचिन्तयाकुलः॥१०॥

*babhūva me vartmani daivayogā-*
*ccharīravaivaśyamataḥ kathaṁ syāt|*
*gayāsu me paitṛkakarmavighnaḥ*
*śreyasyabhūdityaticintayākulaḥ||10||*

*Word for word:* babhuva — has come; me — upon Me; vartmani — on the way; daiva-yogat — by the will of fate; sharira-vaivashyam — weakness of body; atah — so; katham — how; syat — will (it) be (done); gayasu — at Gaya; me — My; paitrika-karma-vighnah — an obstacle to the rite for My father; shreyasi — in a good (work); abhut — has arisen; iti — thus; ati-chintaya — with great anxiety; akulah — troubled.

**10.** "On the way, by the will of fate, My body has grown weak," He thought anxiously. "How now will My rite for My father be performed at Gaya? An obstacle has arisen to a good work."

### Verse 11

ततोऽप्युपायं परिचिन्तयन्स्वयं
ज्वरस्य शान्त्यै द्विजपादसेवनम्।
वरं स विज्ञाय तथोपपादयं-
स्तदम्बुपानं भगवांश्चकार॥११॥

*tato'pyupāyaṁ paricintayansvayaṁ*
*jvarasya śāntyai dvijapādasevanam|*
*varaṁ sa vijñāya tathopapādayaṁ-*
*stadambupānaṁ bhagavāṁścakāra||11||*

*Word for word:* tatah — then; api — indeed; upayam — a remedy; parichintayan — considering; svayam — Himself; jvarasya — of the fever; shantyai — for the cure; dvija-pada-sevanam — service to the feet of brahmanas; varam — the best; sah — He; vijnaya — recognising; tatha — so; upapadayan — arranging; tat-ambu-panam — drinking of that water (from their feet); bhagavan — Bhagavan; chakara — did.

**11.** Then, considering a remedy for the fever Himself, He recognised the service of brahmanas' feet as the best of all, and, arranging it so, Bhagavan drank the water that had washed their feet.

### Verse 12

ये सर्वविप्रा मधुसूदनाश्रया
निरन्तरं कृष्णपदाभिचिन्तकाः।
ततः स्वयं कृष्णजनाभिमानी
तेषां परं पादजलं पपौ प्रभुः॥१२॥

*ye sarvaviprā madhusūdanāśrayā*
*nirantaraṁ kṛṣṇapadābhicintakāḥ|*
*tataḥ svayaṁ kṛṣṇajanābhimānī*
*teṣāṁ paraṁ pādajalaṁ papau prabhuḥ||12||*

*Word for word:* ye — who; sarva-viprah — all the brahmanas; madhusudana-ashrayah — sheltered in Madhusudana; nirantaram — ceaselessly; krishna-pada-abhichintakah — meditating on Krishna's feet; tatah — therefore; svayam — Himself; krishna-jana-abhimani — regarding Himself as one of Krishna's people; tesham — their; param — only; pada-jalam — foot-water; papau — drank; prabhuh — Prabhu.

**12.** All those brahmanas had taken shelter in Madhusudana and ceaselessly meditated on Krishna's feet. That is why Prabhu, who regarded Himself as one of Krishna's people, drank the water from their feet.

### Verse 13

ततो ज्वरस्योपशमो बभूव
तान्दर्शयित्वा द्विजपादभक्तिम्।
जगाम तीर्थं स पुनःपुनाख्यं
चकार तत्र द्विजदेवतार्चनम्॥१३॥

*tato jvarasyopaśamo babhūva*
*tāndarśayitvā dvijapādabhaktim|*
*jagāma tīrthaṁ sa punaḥpunākhyaṁ*
*cakāra tatra dvijadevatārcanam||13||*

*Word for word:* tatah — then; jvarasya — of the fever; upashamah — abatement; babhuva — came; tan — to them; darshayitva — showing; dvija-pada-bhaktim — devotion to the feet of brahmanas; jagama — went; tirtham — to the holy place; sah — He; punahpuna-akhyam — called Punahpuna; chakara — performed; tatra — there; dvija-devata-archanam — worship of brahmanas and gods.

**13.** And the fever abated. Having shown them what devotion to the feet of brahmanas is, He went to the holy place called Punahpuna[^115-6] and there worshipped the brahmanas and the gods.

### Verse 14

ततः समुत्तीर्य नदीं स गच्छं-
स्तीर्थोत्तमे राजगृहे सुपुण्ये।
ब्रह्माख्यकुण्डे पितृदेवपूजां
चकार लोकाननुशिक्षयन्सः॥१४॥

*tataḥ samuttīrya nadīṁ sa gacchaṁ-*
*stīrthottame rājagṛhe supuṇye|*
*brahmākhyakuṇḍe pitṛdevapūjāṁ*
*cakāra lokānanuśikṣayansaḥ||14||*

*Word for word:* tatah — then; samuttirya — crossing; nadim — the river; sah — He; gachchhan — going on; tirtha-uttame — in the best of holy places; rajagrihe — at Rajagriha; su-punye — most sacred; brahma-akhya-kunde — at the pond called Brahma(-kunda); pitri-deva-pujam — worship of forefathers and gods; chakara — performed; lokan — people; anushikshayan — teaching; sah — He.

**14.** Crossing the river and going on, He, teaching people, worshipped the forefathers and the gods at the pond called Brahma-kunda in Rajagriha[^115-7], the most sacred of holy places.

### Verse 15

पत्या स्वमातुः ससुरोऽगमच्छनै-
र्गयां गदाभृच्चरणं दिदृक्षुः॥१५॥

*patyā svamātuḥ sasuro'gamacchanai-*
*rgayāṁ gadābhṛccaraṇaṁ didṛkṣuḥ||15||*

*Word for word:* patya — with (for the sake of) the husband; sva-matuh — of His mother; sa-surah — with the (earthly) gods; agamat — came; shanaih — slowly; gayam — to Gaya; gada-bhrit-charanam — the feet of the Club-bearer; didrikshuh — wishing to see.

**15.** …For the sake of His mother's husband[^115-8] He came slowly, with the gods on earth, to Gaya, wishing to see the feet of the Club-bearer[^115-9].

### Verse 16

तस्मिन्शुभं न्यासिवरं ददर्श
स ईश्वराख्यं हरिपादभक्तम्।
पुरीं परेशः परयात्मभक्त्या
तुष्टं ननामैनमथाब्रवीच्च॥१६॥

*tasminśubhaṁ nyāsivaraṁ dadarśa*
*sa īśvarākhyaṁ haripādabhaktam|*
*purīṁ pareśaḥ parayātmabhaktyā*
*tuṣṭaṁ nanāmainamathābravīcca||16||*

*Word for word:* tasmin — there; shubham — auspicious; nyasi-varam — the best of sannyasis; dadarsha — saw; sah — He; ishvara-akhyam — named Ishvara; hari-pada-bhaktam — devoted to Hari's feet; purim — Puri; para-ishah — the Supreme Lord; paraya — with supreme; atma-bhaktya — heartfelt devotion; tushtam — pleased; nanama — bowed; enam — to him; atha — then; abravit — spoke; cha — and.

**16.** There the Supreme Lord saw the auspicious Ishvara Puri, the best of sannyasis, devoted to Hari's feet. With the deepest devotion of His heart He bowed to him, and he was pleased. Then the Lord said:

### Verse 17

दिष्ट्याद्य दृष्टं भगवन्पदाम्बुजं
तव प्रभो ब्रूहि यथा भवाम्बुधिम्।
निस्तीर्य कृष्णाङ्घ्रिसरोरुहामृतं
पश्यामि तन्मे करुणानिधे स्वयम्॥१७॥

*diṣṭyādya dṛṣṭaṁ bhagavanpadāmbujaṁ*
*tava prabho brūhi yathā bhavāmbudhim|*
*nistīrya kṛṣṇāṅghrisaroruhāmṛtaṁ*
*paśyāmi tanme karuṇānidhe svayam||17||*

*Word for word:* dishtya — by good fortune; adya — today; drishtam — are seen; bhagavan — O revered one; pada-ambujam — the lotus feet; tava — your; prabho — O master; bruhi — tell; yatha — how; bhava-ambudhim — the ocean of worldly existence; nistirya — crossing; krishna-anghri-saroruha-amritam — the nectar of Krishna's lotus feet; pashyami — I may behold (taste); tat — that; me — to me; karuna-nidhe — O treasury of mercy; svayam — yourself.

**17.** "O revered one! By good fortune I have seen your lotus feet today. Tell Me yourself, O master, O treasury of mercy, how I may cross the ocean of worldly existence and taste the nectar of Krishna's lotus feet."

### Verse 18

स इत्थमाकर्ण्य हरेर्वचोऽमृतं
मुदा ददौ मन्त्रवरं मतिज्ञः।
दशाक्षरं प्राप्य स गौरचन्द्रमा-
स्तुष्टाव तं भक्तिविभावितः स्वयम्॥१८॥

*sa itthamākarṇya harervaco'mṛtaṁ*
*mudā dadau mantravaraṁ matijñaḥ|*
*daśākṣaraṁ prāpya sa gauracandramā-*
*stuṣṭāva taṁ bhaktivibhāvitaḥ svayam||18||*

*Word for word:* sah — he; ittham — thus; akarnya — hearing; hareh — of Hari; vachah-amritam — the nectar of words; muda — gladly; dadau — gave; mantra-varam — the best of mantras; mati-jnah — knowing (His) heart; dasha-aksharam — the ten-syllable (mantra); prapya — receiving; sah — He; gaura-chandramah — Gaurachandra; tushtava — praised; tam — him; bhakti-vibhavitah — overwhelmed by devotion; svayam — Himself.

**18.** Hearing these nectarean words of Hari, Puri, who knew His heart, gladly gave Him the best of mantras — the ten-syllable one[^115-10]. Having received it, Gaurachandra Himself, overwhelmed by devotion, praised him:

### Verse 19

न्यासिन्दयालो तव पादसङ्गमा-
त्कृतार्थता मेऽद्य बभूव दुर्लभा।
श्रीकृष्णपादाब्जमधून्मदा च सा
यथा तरिष्यामि दुरन्तसंसृतिम्॥१९॥

*nyāsindayālo tava pādasaṅgamā-*
*tkṛtārthatā me'dya babhūva durlabhā|*
*śrīkṛṣṇapādābjamadhūnmadā ca sā*
*yathā tariṣyāmi durantasaṁsṛtim||19||*

*Word for word:* nyasin — O sannyasi; dayalo — O merciful one; tava — your; pada-sangamat — from contact with the feet; krita-arthata — fulfilment; me — my; adya — today; babhuva — has come; durlabha — rare; shri-krishna-pada-abja-madhu-unmada — intoxicated with the honey of Sri Krishna's lotus feet; cha — and; sa — that; yatha — so that; tarishyami — I shall cross; duranta-samsritim — the endless round of birth and death.

**19.** "O sannyasi, O merciful one! Through contact with your feet I have today attained a rare fulfilment — intoxication with the honey of Sri Krishna's lotus feet, by which I shall cross the endless round of birth and death."

*Thus ends the fifteenth sarga, "The Meeting with Srimad Ishvara Puri" (Shrimad-ishvara-puri-darshana), of the first prakrama of the great poem "Sri Krishna-chaitanya-charitamrita."*

[^115-1]: Vaidyas: the community of physicians, to which Murari Gupta himself belonged.
[^115-2]: Vachaspati is Brihaspati, the preceptor of the gods and the model of eloquence; Kavya is Shukra, the preceptor of the asuras and the model of the poet. The sense: their eloquence and poetry, and the moon's radiance, belong originally to the Lord, and when He came to earth they gave Him back, as it were, what had been deposited with them.
[^115-3]: Rasa is the taste, the inner experience of loving service; rasikas are those able to relish it.
[^115-4]: That is, with brahmanas.
[^115-5]: Mandara is a sacred hill in Bihar (near present-day Bhagalpur), where Madhusudana is worshipped.
[^115-6]: Punahpuna (the present Punpun) is a sacred river on the way to Gaya.
[^115-7]: Rajagriha (present-day Rajgir) is an ancient holy town in Bihar.
[^115-8]: In all witnesses only half of this verse survives. Literally "with His mother's husband," that is, apparently, for the sake of His late father, Jagannatha Mishra; the sense is conjectural.
[^115-9]: The Club-bearer is Gadadhara, Vishnu as worshipped at Gaya; His footprint (Vishnu-pada) is the chief shrine of Gaya.
[^115-10]: The ten-syllable mantra is the mantra of Gopala-Krishna.

## Prakrama 1, Sarga 16. The Journey to Gaya

*Ancestral rites at the holy places of Gaya; Jagannatha Mishra appears to accept the pinda; love awakens at the footprint of Vishnu; a voice from the sky bids the Lord return home; His ecstasy in Navadvipa; a brief glance ahead — sannyasa, Puri, the South, Mathura; the fruit of hearing*

### Verse 1

गुरौ स भक्तिं परिदर्शयन्स्वयं
फल्गुषु चक्रे पितृदेवतार्चनम्।
प्रेतादिशृङ्गे पितृपिण्डदानं
ब्रह्माङ्गुलीरेणुयुतेषु कृत्वा॥१॥

*gurau sa bhaktiṁ paridarśayansvayaṁ*
*phalguṣu cakre pitṛdevatārcanam|*
*pretādiśṛṅge pitṛpiṇḍadānaṁ*
*brahmāṅgulīreṇuyuteṣu kṛtvā||1||*

*Word for word:* gurau — towards the guru; sah — He; bhaktim — devotion; paridarshayan — showing; svayam — Himself; phalgushu — at the Phalgu; chakre — performed; pitri-devata-archanam — worship of forefathers and gods; preta-adi-shringe — on the peak of Preta (Pretashila); pitri-pinda-danam — the offering of pinda to the forefathers; brahma-anguli-renu-yuteshu — on (spots) bearing the dust of Brahma's fingers; kritva — having made.

**1.** Himself showing what devotion to the guru should be, He worshipped the forefathers and the gods at the Phalgu, and on the peak of Pretashila, on spots bearing the dust of Brahma's fingers, offered pindas to the forefathers[^116-1].

### Verse 2

देवान्समभ्यर्च्य ददौ द्विजातये
पितॄन्समुद्दिश्य यथेष्टदक्षिणाम्।
ततोऽवरुह्याशु ययावुदीचीं
पितृक्रियां दक्षिणमानसे च॥२॥

*devānsamabhyarcya dadau dvijātaye*
*pitṝnsamuddiśya yatheṣṭadakṣiṇām|*
*tato'varuhyāśu yayāvudīcīṁ*
*pitṛkriyāṁ dakṣiṇamānase ca||2||*

*Word for word:* devan — the gods; samabhyarchya — having worshipped; dadau — gave; dvijataye — to the brahmana; pitrin — the forefathers; samuddishya — on behalf of; yatha-ishta-dakshinam — as much dakshina as desired; tatah — then; avaruhya — descending; ashu — quickly; yayau — went; udichim — northward; pitri-kriyam — the rite for the forefathers; dakshina-manase — at Dakshina-manasa; cha — and.

**2.** Having worshipped the gods, He gave the brahmanas as much dakshina as they wished on behalf of His forefathers; then He quickly came down and went north. Having performed the ancestral rite at Dakshina-manasa

### Verse 3

कृत्वोत्तरे मानससंज्ञके च
ययौ स जिह्वाचपले द्विजान्वितः।
श्राद्धं पितॄणामथ देवतानां
कृत्वा गयामूर्ध्नि जगाम हृष्टः॥३॥

*kṛtvottare mānasasaṁjñake ca*
*yayau sa jihvācapale dvijānvitaḥ|*
*śrāddhaṁ pitṝṇāmatha devatānāṁ*
*kṛtvā gayāmūrdhni jagāma hṛṣṭaḥ||3||*

*Word for word:* kritva — having performed; uttare manasa-samjnake — at the (pond) called Uttara-manasa; cha — and; yayau — went; sah — He; jihvachapale — to Jihvachapala; dvija-anvitah — with the brahmanas; shraddham — the shraddha; pitrinam — to the forefathers; atha — and; devatanam — to the gods; kritva — having performed; gaya-murdhni — to the head of Gaya; jagama — went; hrishtah — joyful.

**3.** and at the (pond) called Uttara-manasa, He went with the brahmanas to Jihvachapala. Having performed there the shraddha for the forefathers and the gods, He went joyfully to the head of Gaya[^116-2].

### Verse 4

द्विजोत्तमैः षोडशवेदिकायां
चकार पिण्डं पितृकर्मपूर्वकम्।
श्रीमज्जगन्नाथपुरन्दराख्यः
प्रत्यक्षीभूय जगृहे मुदान्वितः॥४॥

*dvijottamaiḥ ṣoḍaśavedikāyāṁ*
*cakāra piṇḍaṁ pitṛkarmapūrvakam|*
*śrīmajjagannāthapurandarākhyaḥ*
*pratyakṣībhūya jagṛhe mudānvitaḥ||4||*

*Word for word:* dvija-uttamaih — with the best of brahmanas; shodasha-vedikayam — at the Sixteen Altars; chakara — made; pindam — the pinda; pitri-karma-purvakam — with the ancestral rite; shrimat-jagannatha-purandara-akhyah — he named Srimad Jagannatha Purandara; pratyakshibhuya — appearing visibly; jagrihe — accepted; muda-anvitah — joyfully.

**4.** At the Sixteen Altars[^116-3], together with the best of brahmanas, He performed the ancestral rite and offered the pinda — and Srimad Jagannatha Purandara, appearing visibly, joyfully accepted it.

### Verse 5

यथा श्रीरामेण हि दत्तपिण्डो
गृहीत आगम्य तदीयपित्रा।
एवं हि सर्वत्र हरेश्चरित्रं
तथापि दुष्प्राप्यतमं यदेतत्॥५॥

*yathā śrīrāmeṇa hi dattapiṇḍo*
*gṛhīta āgamya tadīyapitrā|*
*evaṁ hi sarvatra hareścaritraṁ*
*tathāpi duṣprāpyatamaṁ yadetat||5||*

*Word for word:* yatha — as; shri-ramena — by Sri Rama; hi — indeed; datta-pindah — the pinda offered; grihitah — was accepted; agamya — coming; tadiya-pitra — by his father; evam — so; hi — indeed; sarvatra — everywhere; hareh — of Hari; charitram — the deeds; tatha api — and yet; dushprapyatamam — most rarely attained; yat — which; etat — this.

**5.** Just so, long ago, the pinda offered by Sri Rama was accepted by his father, who came for it[^116-4]. Thus Hari's deeds are alike everywhere — and yet this event is the rarest of all.

### Verse 6

स विष्णुपद्यां हरिपादचिह्नं
दृष्ट्वातिहृष्टो मनसाब्रवीच्च।
कथं हरेः पादपयोजलक्ष्म-
प्रेमोदयो मे न बभूव दृष्ट्वा॥६॥

*sa viṣṇupadyāṁ haripādacihnaṁ*
*dṛṣṭvātihṛṣṭo manasābravīcca|*
*kathaṁ hareḥ pādapayojalakṣma-*
*premodayo me na babhūva dṛṣṭvā||6||*

*Word for word:* sah — He; vishnupadyam — at the Vishnupada; hari-pada-chihnam — the footprint of Hari; drishtva — seeing; ati-hrishtah — overjoyed; manasa — to Himself; abravit — said; cha — and; katham — why; hareh — of Hari; pada-payoja-lakshma — the marks of the lotus foot; prema-udayah — an awakening of love; me — in Me; na — not; babhuva — has come; drishtva — on seeing.

**6.** Seeing the footprint of Hari at the Vishnupada, He was overjoyed, but said to Himself: "Why, on seeing the marks of Hari's lotus foot, have I felt no awakening of love?"

### Verse 7

तस्मिन्क्षणे तस्य बभूव दैवा-

*tasminkṣaṇe tasya babhūva daivā-*

*Word for word:* tasmin kshane — at that moment; tasya — its (the footprint's); babhuva — took place; daivat — by providence; su-shita-toyaih — with very cool water; abhishechanam — a bathing; muhuh — again and again; kampa-urdhva-roma — trembling, His hair on end; bhagavan — Bhagavan; babhuva — became; prema-ambu-dhara-shata-dhauta-vakshah — His chest washed by a hundred streams of tears of love.

**7.** At that moment, by providence, the footprint was bathed again and again with very cool water[^116-5] — and Bhagavan trembled, His hair stood on end, and His chest was washed by a hundred streams of tears of love.

### Verse 8

स विह्वलः कृष्णपदाब्जयुग्म-

त्यक्त्वा गयां गन्तुमियेष रम्यां
मधोर्वनं साधुनिषेवितां ताम्॥८॥

*sa vihvalaḥ kṛṣṇapadābjayugma-*
*premotsavenāśu vimuktasaṅgaḥ|*

*Word for word:* sah — He; vihvalah — beside Himself; krishna-pada-abja-yugma-prema-utsavena — by the festival of love for Krishna's lotus feet; ashu — at once; vimukta-sangah — free of all attachment; tyaktva — leaving; gayam — Gaya; gantum — to go; iyesha — wished; ramyam — lovely; madhoh vanam — to Madhuvana; sadhu-nishevitam — frequented by saints; tam — that.

**8.** Beside Himself with the festival of love for Krishna's lotus feet, at once free of all attachment, He wished to leave Gaya and go to lovely Madhuvana[^116-6], frequented by saints.

### Verse 9

प्राहाशरीरा नवमेघनिस्वना

मधोर्वनं चान्यदपि स्वचेष्टया॥९॥

*prāhāśarīrā navameghanisvanā*
*vāṇī tamāhūya cala svamandiram|*
*tataḥ paraṁ kālavaśena deva*

*Word for word:* praha — said; asharira — bodiless; nava-megha-nisvana — with a sound like a fresh rain-cloud; vani — a voice; tam — Him; ahuya — calling; chala — go; sva-mandiram — to Your home; tatah param — after that; kala-vashena — in due time; deva — O Lord; madhoh vanam — to Madhuvana; cha — and; anyat api — elsewhere too; sva-cheshtaya — by Your own will.

**9.** Then a bodiless voice, deep as a fresh rain-cloud, called Him and said: "Go to Your home. Afterwards, in due time, O Lord, You will go by Your own will both to Madhuvana and elsewhere.

**10.** You are certainly the Lord of all, able in every way to do or not to do. Yet, O Lord, the word spoken by Your servants You must surely make true."

### Verse 11

स इत्थमाकर्ण्य गिरं सुदिव्या-

*sa itthamākarṇya giraṁ sudivyā-*

*Word for word:* sah — He; ittham — such; akarnya — hearing; giram — words; su-divyam — divine; agatya — coming; geham — home; nija-bandhubhih — by His kinsmen; vritah — surrounded; nanama — bowed; matuh — of His mother; charane — at the feet; nipatya — falling; babhuva — became; harsha-ashru-vilochana — her eyes filled with tears of joy; shachi — Shachi.

**11.** Having heard this divine speech, He came home, surrounded by His kinsmen, and fell at His mother's feet in obeisance; and Shachi's eyes filled with tears of joy.

### Verse 12

गृहे वसन्प्रेमविभिन्नधैर्यं

*gṛhe vasanpremavibhinnadhairyaṁ*

*Word for word:* grihe — at home; vasan — living; prema-vibhinna-dhairyam — His composure shattered by love; rudati — weeps; alam — abundantly; rauti — cries out; muhuh muhuh — again and again; svanaih — aloud; sa-vepathuh — trembling; gadgadaya gira — in a faltering voice; lapati — calls; alam — much; hare — O Hari; krishna — O Krishna; hare — O Hari; muda — joyfully; kvachit — at times.

**12.** Living at home, His composure shattered by love, He would weep long and cry out loudly again and again, and at times, trembling, He would joyfully call in a faltering voice: "Hari! Krishna! Hari!"

**13.** At times, with Srivasa, the brahmanas and others, He sang in new ways and danced, full of feeling, and, imitating various avatars, He took delight in this and taught the people.

*nyāsaṁ sa cakre haripādapadme*

**14.** He renounced all action at Hari's lotus feet and became the best of sannyasis. Then, surrounded by great souls headed by Mukunda, dear to Hari, He went to the best of kshetras[^116-7]

### Verse 15

ददर्श देवं पुरुषोत्तमेश्वरं

*dadarśa devaṁ puruṣottameśvaraṁ*

*Word for word:* dadarsha — saw; devam — the Lord; purushottama-ishvaram — the Lord of Purushottama; chiram — for long; chira-ananda-sukha-ati-sat-sukham — the true bliss surpassing everlasting joy and happiness; labdhva — having attained; agamat — went; raghava-deva-nirmitam — built by Lord Raghava; setum — to the bridge; pathi — on the road; prajna-janaih — with wise men; sah — He; sadhubhih — saintly.

**15.** and long beheld the Lord, the Master of Purushottama — the true bliss surpassing everlasting joy and happiness. Having attained this, He went with wise and saintly men along the road to the bridge built by Lord Raghava[^116-8].

तत्र स्थितान्सप्ततमालवृक्षा-

*tatra sthitānsaptatamālavṛkṣā-*

**16.** Embracing the seven tamala trees[^116-9] that stand there, He wept long. Then Prabhu came to Kurma and saw the Lord of the world in the form of a tortoise[^116-10].

**17.** Then He came back to the kshetra called Sri Purushottama and saw the face of Jagannatha. Having stayed there some days, Achyuta went to Mathura, the city of the Enemy of Madhu.

**18.** Reaching the land adorned with the marks of (Krishna's) lotus feet, the Teacher of the world wept, rolling vehemently on the ground, and stayed there some days, eager only to taste the nectar of love.

**19.** Thus, having spread supreme bliss in Madhupuri, Prabhu suddenly left in joy and again, step by step, in the company of saints, came to the supreme abode — the playground of Purushottama.

### Verse 20

श्रुत्वा च तीर्थस्य विधिक्रियां हरे-

देहावसाने विमलां गतिं नरः

**20.** Whoever hears how Hari performed the rites at the holy place gains the greatest fruit of pilgrimage to Gaya; and a man full of faith and complete longing reaches, at the end of the body, a pure destination.

*Thus ends the sixteenth sarga, "The Journey to Gaya" (Gaya-gamana), of the first prakrama of the great poem "Sri Krishna-chaitanya-charitamrita." Thus the first prakrama is complete.*

[^116-1]: The Phalgu is the sacred river of Gaya; Pretashila is a hill near Gaya where pindas (balls of rice) are offered to the forefathers. Its stones, by local tradition, bear the marks of Brahma's fingers. The reading "on the peak of Pretashila" is conjectural.
[^116-2]: Dakshina-manasa, Uttara-manasa and Jihvachapala (Jihvalola) are holy places of Gaya where shraddha is performed. "The head of Gaya" is the spot on the head of the asura Gaya on which Vishnu placed His foot; the shrine of the Vishnupada stands there.
[^116-3]: The Sixteen Altars (Shodasha-vedi) are the place of pinda offerings by the Vishnupada temple.
[^116-4]: Rama's father is Dasharatha.
[^116-5]: Literally "its": apparently the footprint of Vishnu; it may also be understood that the Lord Himself was drenched with cool water.
[^116-6]: Madhuvana, the forest of Madhu, is the region of Mathura (Vraja).
[^116-7]: Verses 14–19 briefly anticipate events described in detail in the following prakramas: the sannyasa, the life in Puri (the kshetra of Purushottama), and the pilgrimages to the South and to Mathura.
[^116-8]: Raghava is Rama; the bridge (Setubandha) is the bridge to Lanka built by Rama.
[^116-9]: The tamala is a tree with dark bark whose colour recalls Krishna.
[^116-10]: Kurma is Kurma-kshetra (Srikurmam) in the South, where Vishnu is worshipped in the form of the Tortoise.

# Prakrama Two

---

## Prakrama 2, Sarga 1. The Manifestation of Ecstasy

*Opening of the second prakrama: Damodara Pandita asks to hear of the Lord's pastimes in Navadvipa; Murari's prayers; Shachi asks her Son for prema; the Lord's ecstatic states in Navadvipa*

### Verse 1

ततः प्रोवाच तच्छ्रुत्वा श्रीदामोदरपण्डितः।
नवद्वीपे किमकरोल्लीलां लीलानिधिः प्रभुः॥१॥

*tataḥ provāca tacchrutvā śrīdāmodarapaṇḍitaḥ|*
*navadvīpe kimakarollīlāṁ līlānidhiḥ prabhuḥ||1||*

*Word for word:* tatah — then; provacha — said; tat — that; shrutva — having heard; shri-damodara-panditah — Sri Damodara Pandita; navadvipe — in Navadvipa; kim — what; akarot — performed; lilam — pastimes; lila-nidhih — the treasury of pastimes; prabhuh — the Lord.

**1.** Having heard this, Sri Damodara Pandita[^201-1] said: "What pastimes did the Lord, the treasury of pastimes, perform in Navadvipa?

### Verse 2

विस्तरेण वदस्वाद्य सर्वश्रुतिरसायनम्।
ततोऽसौ वक्तुमारेभे मुरारिर्हर्षयन्द्विजम्॥२॥

*vistareṇa vadasvādya sarvaśrutirasāyanam|*
*tato'sau vaktumārebhe murārirharṣayandvijam||2||*

*Word for word:* vistarena — in detail; vadasva — tell; adya — now; sarva-shruti-rasayanam — an elixir for every ear; tatah — then; asau — he; vaktum — to speak; arebhe — began; murarih — Murari; harshayan — delighting; dvijam — the brahmana.

**2.** Tell of them now in detail — it is an elixir for every ear." And then Murari, delighting the brahmana, began to speak:

### Verse 3

श्रूयतां महदाश्चर्या कथा संक्षेपतो मम।
नत्वा वक्ष्यामि देवेशचैतन्यचरणाम्बुजम्॥३॥

*śrūyatāṁ mahadāścaryā kathā saṁkṣepato mama|*

*Word for word:* shruyatam — let it be heard; mahat-ashcharya — greatly wondrous; katha — the story; sankshepatah — in brief; mama — my; natva — having bowed; vakshyami — I shall tell; devesha-chaitanya-charana-ambujam — to the lotus feet of Chaitanya, Lord of the gods.

**3.** "Hear my brief account, great and wondrous. Having bowed to the lotus feet of Chaitanya, Lord of the gods, I shall begin."

### Verse 4

चैतन्यचन्द्र तव पादनखेन्दुकान्ति-
रेकादशेन्द्रियगणैः सहजीवकोषम्।
अन्तर्बहिश्च परिपूरय तस्य नित्यं
पुष्णातु नन्दयतु मे शरणागतस्य॥४॥

*caitanyacandra tava pādanakhendukānti-*
*rekādaśendriyagaṇaiḥ sahajīvakoṣam|*

[^201-1]: The poem is framed as a dialogue: Murari Gupta tells Damodara Pandita of the Lord's life. "This" is the account of the first prakrama, which ended with the Lord's return from Gaya.
[^201-2]: The eleven senses are the five organs of knowledge, the five organs of action, and the mind.
[^201-3]: Shuklambara Brahmachari was a poor brahmana of Navadvipa who lived on alms; one of the Lord's first companions.
[^201-4]: A prahara ("watch") is an eighth part of the day and night, about three hours.

*nahi jānāti vedo māmiti niścitameva hi||24||*

*Word for word:* iti — thus; veda-vachah — the words of the Veda; devah — the Lord; hasan eva — laughing; abhyabhashata — recited; na hi — not at all; janati — knows; vedah — the Veda; mam — Me; iti — thus; nishchitam — certain; eva hi — indeed.

**24.** Having recited these words of the Veda with a laugh, the Lord said: "The Veda does not know Me at all — that is certain."

### Verse 25

अम्बष्ठः प्राह भगवन्करुणां कर्तुमर्हसि।
तं प्राह भगवान्देवः प्रेमा मयि दयामयः॥२५॥

*ambaṣṭhaḥ prāha bhagavankaruṇāṁ kartumarhasi|*
*taṁ prāha bhagavāndevaḥ premā mayi dayāmayaḥ||25||*

*Word for word:* ambashthah — the Ambashtha; praha — said; bhagavan — O Bhagavan; karunam — mercy; kartum arhasi — please show; tam — to him; praha — said; bhagavan — Bhagavan; devah — the Lord; prema — love; mayi — for Me; daya-mayah — the merciful.

**25.** The Ambashtha[^202-6] said: "O Bhagavan, be merciful to me!" The merciful Bhagavan answered him: "(May you have) love for Me."

### Verse 26

इत्युक्त्वा स स्मितमुखो जगाम निजमन्दिरम्।
श्रीमान्विश्वम्भरो देवो हरिकीर्तनतत्परः॥२६॥

*ityuktvā sa smitamukho jagāma nijamandiram|*
*śrīmānviśvambharo devo harikīrtanatatparaḥ||26||*

*Word for word:* iti — thus; uktva — having said; sah — He; smita-mukhah — with a smiling face; jagama — went; nija-mandiram — to His own house; shriman — the beautiful; vishvambharah — Vishvambhara; devah — the Lord; hari-kirtana-tatparah — devoted to Hari's kirtana.

**26.** Having said this, the beautiful Lord Vishvambhara, devoted to Hari's kirtana, went home with a smile.

### Verse 27

अपरेद्युः पण्डितस्य श्रीवासस्य पुरे वसन्।
व्याख्यां चकार श्लोकस्य वक्ष्यमाणस्य तच्छृणु॥२७॥

*aparedyuḥ paṇḍitasya śrīvāsasya pure vasan|*
*vyākhyāṁ cakāra ślokasya vakṣyamāṇasya tacchṛṇu||27||*

*Word for word:* aparedyuh — the next day; panditasya — of the Pandita; shrivasasya — Srivasa; pure — in the house; vasan — staying; vyakhyam — an explanation; chakara — gave; shlokasya — of the verse; vakshyamanasya — to be cited; tat — that; shrinu — hear.

**27.** The next day, while at the house of Srivasa Pandita, He explained a verse which I shall now quote — listen:

### Verse 28

हरेर्नाम हरेर्नाम हरेर्नामैव केवलम्।
कलौ नास्त्येव नास्त्येव नास्त्येव गतिरन्यथा॥२८॥

*harernāma harernāma harernāmaiva kevalam|*
*kalau nāstyeva nāstyeva nāstyeva gatiranyathā||28||*

*Word for word:* hareh nama — the name of Hari; hareh nama — the name of Hari; hareh nama eva — the name of Hari alone; kevalam — solely; kalau — in Kali; na asti eva — there is none; na asti eva — there is none; na asti eva — there is none; gatih — way; anyatha — other.

**28.** "The name of Hari, the name of Hari, the name of Hari alone is the only one! In Kali there is no, no, no other way[^202-7]."

### Verse 29

ना पुमानादिपुरुषः कलावस्त्येव रूपवान्।
नामस्वरूपिणं तं तु जानीहि स तु केवलम्॥२९॥

*nā pumānādipuruṣaḥ kalāvastyeva rūpavān|*
*nāmasvarūpiṇaṁ taṁ tu jānīhi sa tu kevalam||29||*

*Word for word:* na — "na" (person); puman — a man; adi-purushah — the Original Person; kalau — in Kali; asti eva — is present indeed; rupavan — possessing form; nama-svarupinam — as having the Name for His form; tam — Him; tu — and; janihi — know; sah — He; tu — and; kevalam — "alone."

**29.** "'Na' is the man, the Original Person, who in Kali is present possessing form. Know, then, that His form is the Name; He is the 'only one'[^202-8].

### Verse 30

वारत्रयं हरेर्नाम दृढार्थं सर्वदेहिनाम्।
एवकारश्च जीवानां पापानां नाशहेतवे॥३०॥

*vāratrayaṁ harernāma dṛḍhārthaṁ sarvadehinām|*
*evakāraśca jīvānāṁ pāpānāṁ nāśahetave||30||*

*Word for word:* vara-trayam — three times; hareh nama — "the name of Hari"; dridha-artham — for confirmation; sarva-dehinam — for all embodied beings; eva-karah — the word "eva"; cha — and; jivanam — of living beings; papanam — of the sins; nasha-hetave — for the destruction.

**30.** Three times 'the name of Hari' — to confirm (the truth) for all embodied beings; and the word 'eva' ('alone') — to destroy the sins of living beings.

### Verse 31

सर्वतत्त्वप्रकाशार्थं केवलं मन्यते च हि।
प्रारब्धकर्मनिर्वाणं कथ्यतेऽद्वैतवादिभिः॥३१॥

*sarvatattvaprakāśārthaṁ kevalaṁ manyate ca hi|*
*prārabdhakarmanirvāṇaṁ kathyate'dvaitavādibhiḥ||31||*

*Word for word:* sarva-tattva-prakasha-artham — as revealing all truths; kevalam — "kevalam"; manyate — is understood; cha hi — indeed; prarabdha-karma-nirvanam — the extinction of karma already bearing fruit; kathyate — is said; advaita-vadibhih — by the proponents of non-duality.

**31.** 'The only one' is understood as revealing all truths; whereas the proponents of non-duality say it is the extinction of karma already bearing fruit.

### Verse 32

भवेदिति च बोधार्थं कैवल्यं केवलं स्मृतम्।
कृष्णप्रेमरसास्वादप्रापकं करुणामयम्॥३२॥

*bhavediti ca bodhārthaṁ kaivalyaṁ kevalaṁ smṛtam|*
*kṛṣṇapremarasāsvādaprāpakaṁ karuṇāmayam||32||*

*Word for word:* bhavet — "may it be"; iti — thus; cha — and; bodha-artham — in order to understand; kaivalyam — "kaivalya"; kevalam — "kevalam"; smritam — is held to be; krishna-prema-rasa-asvada-prapakam — bestowing the taste of the rasa of love for Krishna; karuna-mayam — full of mercy.

**32.** Supplying 'may it be,' they take 'the only one' to mean liberation, kaivalya; but (the Name) is full of mercy and bestows the taste of the rasa of love for Krishna.

### Verse 33

तत्स्वरूपं हरेर्नाम योऽन्यदेव वदेत्पुमान्।
तस्य नास्त्येव नास्त्येव गतिरित्यवदत्स्वयम्॥३३॥

*tatsvarūpaṁ harernāma yo'nyadeva vadetpumān|*
*tasya nāstyeva nāstyeva gatirityavadatsvayam||33||*

*Word for word:* tat-svarupam — His very form; hareh nama — the name of Hari; yah — who; anyat eva — otherwise; vadet — says; puman — a man; tasya — for him; na asti eva — there is none; na asti eva — there is none; gatih — way; iti — thus; avadat — said; svayam — Himself.

**33.** The name of Hari is His very form. Whoever says otherwise has no, no way," — so He Himself said.

### Verse 34

इत्यसौ शूकरो ब्रूते सर्वदेवमयः पुमान्।
इत्युक्त्वा नर्तनं चक्रे कीर्तनं च विशेषतः॥३४॥

*ityasau śūkaro brūte sarvadevamayaḥ pumān|*
*ityuktvā nartanaṁ cakre kīrtanaṁ ca viśeṣataḥ||34||*

*Word for word:* iti — thus; asau — this; shukarah — Boar; brute — says; sarva-deva-mayah — comprising all the gods; puman — the Person; iti — thus; uktva — having said; nartanam — dance; chakre — performed; kirtanam — kirtana; cha — and; visheshatah — especially.

**34.** "So says this Boar, the Person who comprises all the gods" — having said this, He began to dance, and above all to sing kirtana.

### Verse 35

एतद्यः शृणुयान्नित्यं कीर्तयेद्वा समाहितः।
हरौ प्रेमा भवेत्तस्य विपाप्मा च भवेद्ध्रुवम्॥३५॥

*etadyaḥ śṛṇuyānnityaṁ kīrtayedvā samāhitaḥ|*
*harau premā bhavettasya vipāpmā ca bhaveddhruvam||35||*

*Word for word:* etat — this; yah — who; shrinuyat — hears; nityam — constantly; kirtayet — recounts; va — or; samahitah — attentively; harau — for Hari; prema — love; bhavet — will be; tasya — his; vipapma — sinless; cha — and; bhavet — will become; dhruvam — surely.

**35.** Whoever constantly and attentively hears or recounts this will surely come to love Hari and will become free from sin;

### Verse 36

श्रीमच्चैतन्यपादाब्जे प्रभुबुद्धिर्दृढा भवेत्।
अन्ते चैतन्यदेवस्य स्मृतिर्भवति शाश्वती॥३६॥

*śrīmaccaitanyapādābje prabhubuddhirdṛḍhā bhavet|*
*ante caitanyadevasya smṛtirbhavati śāśvatī||36||*

*Word for word:* shrimach-chaitanya-pada-abje — at the lotus feet of Sri Chaitanya; prabhu-buddhih — the awareness (of Him) as Lord; dridha — firm; bhavet — will be; ante — at the end; chaitanya-devasya — of Chaitanya-deva; smritih — remembrance; bhavati — comes; shashvati — unfailing.

**36.** at the lotus feet of Sri Chaitanya his awareness that He is the Lord will become firm, and at the end of life unfailing remembrance of Chaitanya-deva will come to him.

*Thus ends the second sarga, "Absorption in the Boar" (Varaha-avesha), in the description of Chaitanya's descent, of the second prakrama of the great poem "Sri Krishna-chaitanya-charitamrita."*

[^202-1]: Kamala is Lakshmi, the consort of Vishnu.
[^202-2]: Sri Rama (Ramai Pandita) was Srivasa's younger brother.
[^202-3]: A vaidya is a member of the physician caste. Mukunda Datta was a vaidya; "another vaidya" is apparently the author himself, Murari Gupta.
[^202-4]: Bhagavad-gita 10.15.
[^202-5]: Shvetashvatara Upanishad 3.19 (as the poem reads it).
[^202-6]: Ambashtha is the name of the vaidya caste; here, Murari.
[^202-7]: A verse of the Brihan-naradiya Purana. In verses 29–33 the Lord comments on its words.
[^202-8]: "Na" (nā) means "man, person"; the explanation apparently plays on the beginning of the word nama ("name"). The sense of verses 29–32 is unclear in places; the translation is tentative.

## Prakrama 2, Sarga 3. Dispelling the Clouds

*The gods come to serve the Lord; He grants boons to His devotees and prema to Shuklambara; Gadadhara's service; the Lord dispels the clouds that hindered the kirtana, while the gods look on from the sky*

### Verse 1

अथ प्रविष्टो निजवेश्मनि प्रभु-
र्बभौ निशानाथसहस्ररोचिषा।
उवाच चात्रैत्य वसन्ति के जना-
श्चतुर्मुखः षण्मुखपञ्चवक्त्रिणः॥१॥

*atha praviṣṭo nijaveśmani prabhu-*
*rbabhau niśānāthasahasrarociṣā|*
*uvāca cātraitya vasanti ke janā-*
*ścaturmukhaḥ ṣaṇmukhapañcavaktriṇaḥ||1||*

*Word for word:* atha — then; pravishtah — having entered; nija-veshmani — His own house; prabhuh — the Lord; babhau — shone; nisha-natha-sahasra-rochisha — with the light of a thousand moons; uvacha — said; cha — and; atra — here; etya — having come; vasanti — are staying; ke — who; janah — beings; chatur-mukhah — four-faced; shan-mukha-pancha-vaktrinah — six-faced and five-faced.

**1.** Then the Lord entered His house and shone with the light of a thousand moons. And He said: "Who are these beings who have come and are staying here — the four-faced one, the six-faced and the five-faced?[^203-1]"

### Verse 2

श्रीवासनामा द्विजवर्यसत्तमः
श्रुत्वावदत्तं विबुधाः समागताः।
ब्रह्मेश्वरौ षड्वदनादयः प्रभो
त्वां सेवितुं प्रेमरसामृताब्धिम्॥२॥

*śrīvāsanāmā dvijavaryasattamaḥ*
*śrutvāvadattaṁ vibudhāḥ samāgatāḥ|*
*brahmeśvarau ṣaḍvadanādayaḥ prabho*
*tvāṁ sevituṁ premarasāmṛtābdhim||2||*

*Word for word:* shrivasa-nama — named Srivasa; dvija-varya-sattamah — the best of the best brahmanas; shrutva — having heard; avadat — said; tam — to Him; vibudhah — the gods; samagatah — have come; brahma-ishvarau — Brahma and Ishvara (Shiva); shad-vadana-adayah — the Six-faced and others; prabho — O Lord; tvam — You; sevitum — to serve; prema-rasa-amrita-abdhim — the ocean of the nectar of the rasa of love.

**2.** Hearing this, the best of the best brahmanas, named Srivasa, said to Him: "The gods have come — Brahma and Shiva, the Six-faced one and others — O Lord, to serve You, the ocean of the nectar of the rasa of love."

### Verse 3

ततः परदिने प्राप्ते शुद्धदेवो वरासने।
उपविश्य स्वभक्तस्य गात्रे पद्भ्यां समस्पृशत्॥३॥

*tataḥ paradine prāpte śuddhadevo varāsane|*
*upaviśya svabhaktasya gātre padbhyāṁ samaspṛśat||3||*

*Word for word:* tatah — then; para-dine prapte — when the next day came; shuddha-devah — the pure Lord; vara-asane — on an excellent seat; upavishya — seated; sva-bhaktasya — of His devotees; gatre — the bodies; padbhyam — with His feet; samasprishat — touched.

**3.** The next day the pure Lord sat on an exalted seat and touched the bodies of His devotees with His feet.

### Verse 4

श्रीवासपण्डिताद्यास्ते प्रणम्य शिरसा हरिम्।
वव्रुस्तच्चरणे भक्तिं प्रेमरूपां सुदुर्लभाम्॥४॥

*śrīvāsapaṇḍitādyāste praṇamya śirasā harim|*
*vavrustaccaraṇe bhaktiṁ premarūpāṁ sudurlabhām||4||*

*Word for word:* shrivasa-pandita-adyah — Srivasa Pandita and the others; te — they; pranamya — having bowed; shirasa — with their heads; harim — to Hari; vavruh — chose (asked for); tat-charane — for His feet; bhaktim — devotion; prema-rupam — in the form of love; sudurlabham — most rare.

**4.** Srivasa Pandita and the others, bowing their heads to Hari, asked for devotion to His feet — devotion in the form of love, so very rare.

### Verse 5

ददौ तेभ्यो वरान्देवो यथेष्टान्भक्तवत्सलः।
शुक्लाम्बरब्रह्मचारी तमूचे पुरुषर्षभम्॥५॥

*dadau tebhyo varāndevo yatheṣṭānbhaktavatsalaḥ|*
*śuklāmbarabrahmacārī tamūce puruṣarṣabham||5||*

*Word for word:* dadau — gave; tebhyah — to them; varan — boons; devah — the Lord; yatha-ishtan — as they wished; bhakta-vatsalah — loving to His devotees; shuklambara-brahmachari — Shuklambara Brahmachari; tam — to Him; uche — said; purusha-rishabham — the bull among men.

**5.** The Lord, loving to His devotees, granted them the boons they desired. Then Shuklambara Brahmachari said to Him, the bull among men:

### Verse 6

भगवन्मथुरां द्वारावतीं गत्वातिदुःखितम्।
मां ज्ञात्वा देहि मे प्रेमभक्तिं तं प्राह स प्रभुः॥६॥

*bhagavanmathurāṁ dvārāvatīṁ gatvātiduḥkhitam|*
*māṁ jñātvā dehi me premabhaktiṁ taṁ prāha sa prabhuḥ||6||*

*Word for word:* bhagavan — O Bhagavan; mathuram — to Mathura; dvaravatim — to Dvaravati; gatva — having gone; ati-duhkhitam — very unhappy; mam — me; jnatva — knowing; dehi — give; me — to me; prema-bhaktim — loving devotion; tam — to him; praha — said; sah — that; prabhuh — Lord.

**6.** "O Bhagavan, I have been to Mathura and to Dvaravati, and still I am very unhappy. Knowing this, give me loving devotion." The Lord answered him:

### Verse 7

जम्बुकाः किं न गच्छन्ति तत्र किं तेन मे भवेत्।
तच्छ्रुत्वैवापतद्भूमौ तमुवाच जनार्दनः॥७॥

*jambukāḥ kiṁ na gacchanti tatra kiṁ tena me bhavet|*
*tacchrutvaivāpatadbhūmau tamuvāca janārdanaḥ||7||*

*Word for word:* jambukah — jackals; kim na — do not; gachchhanti — go; tatra — there; kim — what; tena — by that; me — to Me; bhavet — would be; tat — that; shrutva eva — just on hearing; apatat — he fell; bhumau — to the ground; tam — to him; uvacha — said; janardanah — Janardana.

**7.** "Do not jackals go there too? What is that to Me?" On hearing this he fell to the ground, and Janardana said to him:

### Verse 8

भवत्वद्यैव ते प्रेमा तदा तत्क्षणमेव हि।
रुरोद चरणे विष्णोर्निपत्य प्रेमविह्वलः॥८॥

*bhavatvadyaiva te premā tadā tatkṣaṇameva hi|*
*ruroda caraṇe viṣṇornipatya premavihvalaḥ||8||*

*Word for word:* bhavatu — let there be; adya eva — this very day; te — for you; prema — love; tada — then; tat-kshanam eva hi — at that very moment; ruroda — wept; charane — at the feet; vishnoh — of Vishnu; nipatya — having fallen; prema-vihvalah — overwhelmed by love.

**8.** "Let there be love in you this very day!" — and at that very moment, overwhelmed by love, he fell at the feet of Vishnu and wept.

### Verse 9

ततस्ते हृष्टमनसस्तेन सार्धं मुदान्विताः।
जगुः कृष्णस्य गीतानि नामानि च मुहुर्मुहुः॥९॥

*tataste hṛṣṭamanasastena sārdhaṁ mudānvitāḥ|*
*jaguḥ kṛṣṇasya gītāni nāmāni ca muhurmuhuḥ||9||*

*Word for word:* tatah — then; te — they; hrishta-manasah — with exultant hearts; tena sardham — together with Him; muda-anvitah — joyful; jaguh — sang; krishnasya — of Krishna; gitani — songs; namani — names; cha — and; muhur muhuh — again and again.

**9.** Then all of them, exultant at heart, joyfully sang with Him songs of Krishna, and His names again and again.

### Verse 10

गदाधरो महाप्राज्ञो ब्राह्मणः सत्कुलोद्भवः।
प्रेमभक्तश्च तत्पादसन्निकर्षेऽभितिष्ठति॥१०॥

*gadādharo mahāprājño brāhmaṇaḥ satkulodbhavaḥ|*
*premabhaktaśca tatpādasannikarṣe'bhitiṣṭhati||10||*

*Word for word:* gadadharah — Gadadhara; maha-prajnah — very wise; brahmanah — a brahmana; sat-kula-udbhavah — born of a noble family; prema-bhaktah — a loving devotee; cha — and; tat-pada-sannikarshe — near His feet; abhitishthati — remains.

**10.** The very wise Gadadhara, a brahmana of noble family and a loving devotee, always stayed near His feet.

### Verse 11

तेन सार्धं रजन्यां स तिष्ठन्नूचे शुभाक्षरम्।
दातव्यं भवता प्रातर्वैष्णवेभ्यः प्रसादकम्॥११॥

*tena sārdhaṁ rajanyāṁ sa tiṣṭhannūce śubhākṣaram|*
*dātavyaṁ bhavatā prātarvaiṣṇavebhyaḥ prasādakam||11||*

*Word for word:* tena sardham — with him; rajanyam — at night; sah — He; tishthan — staying; uche — spoke; shubha-aksharam — auspicious words; datavyam — should be given; bhavata — by you; pratah — in the morning; vaishnavebhyah — to the Vaishnavas; prasadakam — (My) prasada.

**11.** One night, while with him, the Lord spoke auspicious words: "In the morning you will give My prasada to the Vaishnavas."

### Verse 12

इत्युक्त्वा गात्रमाल्यानि ददौ तस्य करे हरिः।
ततः प्रभाते विमले ते सर्वे समुपागताः॥१२॥

*ityuktvā gātramālyāni dadau tasya kare hariḥ|*
*tataḥ prabhāte vimale te sarve samupāgatāḥ||12||*

*ye'nekajanmakṛtapuṇyasamudrasaṁkhyā-*

**27.** Those whose merits, earned over many births, are countless as the waters of the ocean, now utterly at peace, dance together with Lord Krishna, covered with thrills of joy and tears, like the happy gods in heaven with the Splitter of mountains[^203-5].

*Thus ends the third sarga, "Dispelling the Clouds" (Megha-nivarana), of the second prakrama of the great poem "Sri Krishna-chaitanya-charitamrita."*

[^203-1]: The four-faced one is Brahma; the six-faced is Skanda (Karttikeya), Shiva's son; the five-faced is Shiva.
[^203-2]: The river of the gods is the Ganga.
[^203-3]: The mandira is a pair of small brass cymbals that keep the rhythm in kirtana.
[^203-4]: That is, the auspicious "ulu-ulu" sound with which Bengali women greet a festive occasion.
[^203-5]: The Splitter of mountains is Indra, king of the gods.

## Prakrama 2, Sarga 4. Immersion in the Heavenly River

*Shuklambara's ecstasy; the Lord's dances and play; the parable of the conjurer; instructions to Mukunda and Murari; the service of Srivasa and Rama; the Lord bathes in the Ganga after hearing Krishna's name reviled*

### Verse 1

तत्र शुक्लाम्बरो नाम द्विजो रोदिति नित्यशः।
पतित्वा दण्डवद्भूमौ वदन्नेवं मुहुर्मुहुः॥१॥

*tatra śuklāmbaro nāma dvijo roditi nityaśaḥ|*
*patitvā daṇḍavadbhūmau vadannevaṁ muhurmuhuḥ||1||*

*Word for word:* tatra — there; shuklambarah nama — named Shuklambara; dvijah — the brahmana; roditi — weeps; nityashah — constantly; patitva — falling; dandavat — like a stick; bhumau — to the ground; vadan — saying; evam — thus; muhur muhuh — again and again.

**1.** The brahmana named Shuklambara wept there constantly; falling to the ground like a stick, he said again and again:

### Verse 2

नवद्वीपस्तु मथुरा कृता तात त्वयाधुना।

*navadvīpastu mathurā kṛtā tāta tvayādhunā|*
*iti saṁvilapanbhūmau roditi premavihvalaḥ||2||*

*Word for word:* navadvipah — Navadvipa; tu — indeed; mathura — into Mathura; krita — has been made; tata — O dear one; tvaya — by You; adhuna — now; iti — thus; samvilapan — lamenting; bhumau — on the ground; roditi — weeps; prema-vihvalah — overwhelmed by love.

**2.** "Now You have made Navadvipa into Mathura[^204-1], O dear one!" — and, lamenting thus, he wept on the ground, overwhelmed by love.

### Verse 3

वयस्यांसे विनिक्षिप्तकरो नृत्यति कर्हिचित्।
क्वचिद्रोमाञ्चिततनुः कल्पते परमः पुमान्॥३॥

*vayasyāṁse vinikṣiptakaro nṛtyati karhicit|*

**3.** Sometimes the Supreme Person danced with His hand on a friend's shoulder, and sometimes the hair of His body stood on end.

*kvacidīśvarabhāvena bhṛtyebhyaḥ pradadau varān|*
*evaṁ nānāvidhākārairnṛtya~llokānaśikṣayat||4||*

*Word for word:* kvachit — sometimes; ishvara-bhavena — in the mood of the Lord; bhrityebhyah — to His servants; pradadau — gave; varan — boons; evam — thus; nana-vidha-akaraih — in manifold forms; nrityan — dancing; lokan — the people; ashikshayat — taught.

*kadācitsvajanaskandhamāruhya harṣayanvibhuḥ|*

**6.** On another day He sat on the ground and, making all the quarters resound with the clapping of His hands, said: "Look, here is a conjurer's trick!

### Verse 7

पश्य पश्याद्भुतं बीजं भूमौ संरोपितं मया।

*paśya paśyādbhutaṁ bījaṁ bhūmau saṁropitaṁ mayā|*
*paśya paśyāṅkuro jāto nimiṣeṇa taruḥ punaḥ||7||*

*Word for word:* pashya pashya — look, look; adbhutam — wondrous; bijam — seed; bhumau — in the ground; samropitam — planted; maya — by Me; pashya pashya — look, look; ankurah — a sprout; jatah — has appeared; nimishena — in the twinkling of an eye; taruh — a tree; punah — then.

*jātaṁ paśyāsya puṣpaughaṁ paśya paśya phalaṁ punaḥ|*
*jātaṁ paśya phalaṁ pakvaṁ tasya saṁgrahaṇaṁ punaḥ||8||*

*Word for word:* jatam — come forth; pashya — look; asya — on it; pushpa-augham — a mass of flowers; pashya pashya — look, look; phalam — fruit; punah — then; jatam — has appeared; pashya — look; phalam — the fruit; pakvam — ripe; tasya — its; sangrahanam — gathering; punah — then.

### Verse 9

फलं वृक्षोऽपि नास्त्येव क्षणान्मायाकृतं यतः।
प्रान्तरे तु कृतं ह्येवं न किञ्चिदपि लभ्यते॥९॥

*phalaṁ vṛkṣo'pi nāstyeva kṣaṇānmāyākṛtaṁ yataḥ|*
*prāntare tu kṛtaṁ hyevaṁ na kiñcidapi labhyate||9||*

*Word for word:* phalam — fruit; vrikshah — tree; api — also; na asti eva — there is none at all; kshanat — in a moment; maya-kritam — made by maya; yatah — since; prantare — in a deserted place; tu — but; kritam — done; hi — indeed; evam — thus; na kinchit api — nothing at all; labhyate — is gained.

**9.** Yet there is no fruit and no tree at all, for it is all made in a moment by maya; and if such a thing is shown in a deserted place, nothing is gained.

### Verse 10

ईश्वरस्याग्रतः कृत्वा धनं विपुलमश्नुते।

*īśvarasyāgrataḥ kṛtvā dhanaṁ vipulamaśnute|*

**10.** But by showing it before a lord, (the conjurer) gains abundant wealth. So too every work done by maya is fruitless in itself;

*Word for word:* pathet — reads; yah — who; ittham — thus; dyunadi-nimajjanam — the immersion in the heavenly river; hareh — of Hari; labhet — will obtain; sah api — he; kratoh — of a sacrifice; phalam — the fruit; narah — the man; harau — for Hari; cha — and; bhaktim — devotion; vimalam — pure; smritim — remembrance; cha — and; prapnoti — obtains; shrinvan — hearing; api — even; tat-phalam — that fruit; narah — a man.

**35.** Whoever reads thus of Hari's immersion in the heavenly river will obtain the fruit of a sacrifice; and even one who hears it obtains that fruit — pure devotion to Hari and remembrance of Him.

*Thus ends the fourth sarga, "Immersion in the Heavenly River" (Dyunadi-majjana), of the second prakrama of the great poem "Sri Krishna-chaitanya-charitamrita."*

[^204-2]: Mukunda Datta, the celebrated kirtana singer; Ambashtha is the caste of the vaidyas (physicians).
[^204-3]: A verse of the Padma Purana, also quoted in the Chaitanya-charitamrita (Madhya 9.29).
[^204-4]: Literally, "perform the abhisheka (consecration) into the office of servant," as at a royal coronation.
[^204-5]: Verse 24 is syntactically unclear; the translation is tentative. The Lord's reply (vv. 25–26) is understood as His blessing on Murari to tell of His descent — that is, to compose this poem.
[^204-6]: Kapila is the sage, a descent of Vishnu, the teacher of the Sankhya doctrine.
[^204-7]: The heavenly river is the Ganga.

## Prakrama 2, Sarga 5. The Telling of Ecstasy

*The Lord goes with His devotees to Advaita in Shantipura; their meeting; a discourse on bhakti in the Kali age; a non-Vaishnava at the festival; pastimes in Advaita's house; instruction in jnana-yoga and the praise of pure devotion*

### Verse 1

ततो जगाम पुर्यां स श्रीवासादिभिरन्वितः।
अद्वैताचार्यवर्यस्य भक्तस्य दर्शनोत्सुकः॥१॥

*tato jagāma puryāṁ sa śrīvāsādibhiranvitaḥ|*
*advaitācāryavaryasya bhaktasya darśanotsukaḥ||1||*

*Word for word:* tatah — then; jagama — went; puryam — to the town; sah — He; shrivasa-adibhih — by Srivasa and others; anvitah — accompanied; advaita-acharya-varyasya — of Advaita, the best of acharyas; bhaktasya — of the devotee; darshana-utsukah — eager for the sight.

**1.** Then, accompanied by Srivasa and others, He set out for the town, eager to see His devotee Advaita, the best of acharyas.

### Verse 2

गच्छन्पथि मुहुर्गायन्हरेर्गीतं मुदान्वितः।
क्वचिन्नृत्यति नृत्यद्भिः स्वजनैः सह स प्रभुः॥२॥

*gacchanpathi muhurgāyanharergītaṁ mudānvitaḥ|*
*kvacinnṛtyati nṛtyadbhiḥ svajanaiḥ saha sa prabhuḥ||2||*

*Word for word:* gachchhan — going; pathi — on the road; muhuh — again and again; gayan — singing; hareh — of Hari; gitam — a song; muda-anvitah — joyful; kvachit — at times; nrityati — dances; nrityadbhih — dancing; svajanaih saha — with His own people; sah — that; prabhuh — Lord.

**2.** On the way the Lord, full of joy, sang songs of Hari again and again, and at times He broke into dance together with His own people, who danced as well.

### Verse 3

ततो गत्वा पपातोर्व्यामाचार्यस्य समीपतः।
दण्डवद्वैष्णवं विष्णुं मन्यमानोऽनुशिक्षयन्॥३॥

*tato gatvā papātorvyāmācāryasya samīpataḥ|*
*daṇḍavadvaiṣṇavaṁ viṣṇuṁ manyamāno'nuśikṣayan||3||*

*Word for word:* tatah — then; gatva — having come; papata — fell; urvyam — on the earth; acharyasya — of the Acharya; samipatah — near; dandavat — like a stick; vaishnavam — a Vaishnava; vishnum — as Vishnu; manyamanah — regarding; anushikshayan — teaching.

**3.** On arriving, He fell to the earth like a stick before the Acharya: regarding a Vaishnava as Vishnu Himself, He taught this to others.

### Verse 4

तं दृष्ट्वा सहसोत्थायाचार्यस्तु तत्समीपतः।
गत्वा पपात भूमौ स सम्भ्रमेण जगद्गुरुः॥४॥

*taṁ dṛṣṭvā sahasotthāyācāryastu tatsamīpataḥ|*
*gatvā papāta bhūmau sa sambhrameṇa jagadguruḥ||4||*

*Word for word:* tam — Him; drishtva — seeing; sahasa — at once; utthaya — rising; acharyah — the Acharya; tu — and; tat-samipatah — near Him; gatva — going; papata — fell; bhumau — on the ground; sah — he; sambhramena — in reverent agitation; jagat-guruh — the teacher of the world.

**4.** Seeing Him, the Acharya, the teacher of the world, at once rose, came up to Him in reverent agitation, and he too fell to the ground.

### Verse 5

अन्योन्यालिङ्गनं कृत्वा प्रेमोत्कण्ठौ बभूवतुः।
कम्पाश्रुपुलकाद्यैस्तु परिपूर्णस्वविग्रहौ॥५॥

*anyonyāliṅganaṁ kṛtvā premotkaṇṭhau babhūvatuḥ|*
*kampāśrupulakādyaistu paripūrṇasvavigrahau||5||*

*Word for word:* anyonya-alinganam — a mutual embrace; kritva — having made; prema-utkanthau — longing in love; babhuvatuh — both became; kampa-ashru-pulaka-adyaih — with trembling, tears, thrilling of the hair and the rest; tu — and; paripurna-sva-vigrahau — their bodies filled.

**5.** They clasped each other in an embrace, and both were seized by the longing of love: their bodies were filled with trembling, tears, the thrill of the hair and the other signs of ecstasy.

### Verse 6

उपविश्य ततो देवः कथां चक्रे हरेः प्रियाम्।
मनोहरां पापहरां मुक्तिप्रेमफलप्रदाम्॥६॥

*upaviśya tato devaḥ kathāṁ cakre hareḥ priyām|*
*manoharāṁ pāpaharāṁ muktipremaphalapradām||6||*

*Word for word:* upavishya — sitting; tatah — then; devah — the Lord; katham — a discourse; chakre — made; hareh — about Hari; priyam — dear; manoharam — captivating the mind; papa-haram — taking away sin; mukti-prema-phala-pradam — bestowing the fruits of liberation and love.

**6.** Then, sitting down, the Lord began a heart-endearing discourse on Hari — captivating the mind, taking away sin, bestowing the fruits of liberation and love.

### Verse 7

ततोऽद्वैतोऽब्रवीद्वाक्यं भक्तिर्नास्ति कलौ क्षितौ।
इति मूढा वदन्ते ये ते पश्यन्त्वद्य चक्षुषा॥७॥

*tato'dvaito'bravīdvākyaṁ bhaktirnāsti kalau kṣitau|*
*iti mūḍhā vadante ye te paśyantvadya cakṣuṣā||7||*

*Word for word:* tatah — then; advaitah — Advaita; abravit — spoke; vakyam — a word; bhaktih — devotion; na asti — there is no; kalau — in Kali; kshitau — on earth; iti — thus; mudhah — fools; vadante — say; ye — who; te — they; pashyantu — let them see; adya — today; chakshusha — with their eyes.

**7.** Advaita then said: "Those fools who claim that in the Kali age there is no devotion on earth — let them see it today with their own eyes!"

### Verse 8

तच्छ्रुत्वा भगवानाह किञ्चित्प्रस्फुरिताधरः।
भक्तिश्चेन्नास्ति नृहरेः किं तदास्ति क्षिताविह॥८॥

*tacchrutvā bhagavānāha kiñcitprasphuritādharaḥ|*
*bhaktiścennāsti nṛhareḥ kiṁ tadāsti kṣitāviha||8||*

*Word for word:* tat — that; shrutva — hearing; bhagavan — Bhagavan; aha — said; kinchit — slightly; prasphurita-adharah — His lips trembling; bhaktih — devotion; chet — if; na asti — there is not; nrihareh — to Nrihari; kim — what; tada — then; asti — is there; kshitau — on earth; iha — here.

**8.** Hearing this, Bhagavan, His lips trembling slightly, said: "If there is no devotion to Nrihari, what then is there at all, here on earth?

### Verse 9

भक्तिरेवास्ति संसारे सर्वसारा सुखावहा।
सा नास्तीति च यो ब्रूते जन्म तस्य निरर्थकम्॥९॥

*bhaktirevāsti saṁsāre sarvasārā sukhāvahā|*
*sā nāstīti ca yo brūte janma tasya nirarthakam||9||*

*Word for word:* bhaktih — devotion; eva — alone; asti — is; samsare — in the world; sarva-sara — the essence of all; sukha-avaha — bringing happiness; sa — it; na asti — is not; iti — that; cha — and; yah — who; brute — says; janma — birth; tasya — his; nirarthakam — meaningless.

**9.** Devotion alone exists in this world — the essence of all, the bringer of happiness. And whoever says that it does not exist has been born in vain.

### Verse 10

तस्मात्कृष्णे भक्तिरास्ते सुप्रसन्ना सनातनी।
यस्य स्यात्कर्मबन्धश्च नश्येत्प्रेमा हरौ भवेत्॥१०॥

*tasmātkṛṣṇe bhaktirāste suprasannā sanātanī|*
*yasya syātkarmabandhaśca naśyetpremā harau bhavet||10||*

*Word for word:* tasmat — therefore; krishne — for Krishna; bhaktih — devotion; aste — abides; su-prasanna — serene; sanatani — eternal; yasya — whose; syat — it may be; karma-bandhah — the bondage of karma; cha — and; nashyet — will perish; prema — love; harau — for Hari; bhavet — will arise.

**10.** And so devotion to Krishna abides — serene and eternal; and for one who has it, the bonds of karma fall away and love for Hari is born."

### Verse 11

ततोऽवदच्छ्रीनिवासो दृष्ट्वा कञ्चिदवैष्णवम्।

*tato'vadacchrīnivāso dṛṣṭvā kañcidavaiṣṇavam|*

**11.** Then Srinivasa, noticing in Hari's assembly, right in front, a certain brahmana who was plainly no Vaishnava, said in distress:

### Verse 12

विघ्नं कृष्णोत्सवे कर्तुं द्विजोऽयं समुपागतः।

*vighnaṁ kṛṣṇotsave kartuṁ dvijo'yaṁ samupāgataḥ|*

**12.** "This brahmana has come to disrupt Krishna's festival." Hearing this, Bhagavan replied: "He will not come in here.

### Verse 13

नास्त्यत्र तव विप्रेन्द्र चिन्ता काचित्सुखी भव।

**13.** Have no anxiety over this, O best of brahmanas; be happy: bewildered by Vishnu's maya, that brahmana has not come here at all."

### Verse 14

स्वयं शान्तिपुरं गत्वा दृष्ट्वाद्वैतमहेश्वरम्।

*svayaṁ śāntipuraṁ gatvā dṛṣṭvādvaitamaheśvaram|*

**14.** Having come Himself to Shantipura and seen Advaita, the great lord[^205-1], the Lord, telling of Krishna's majesty, was wholly filled with Him.

*tataḥ krīḍāparo bhūtvā śrīvāsasyāṁsadeśake|*

### Verse 16

**16.** placing His lotus feet in the lap of Sri Rama Pandita[^205-2], Hari rejoiced with them in the presence of Srimad Advaita Acharya.

### Verse 17

तत्र भुक्त्वा वरान्नं स चन्दनेनानुलेप्य च।

### Verse 19

[^205-1]: Advaita Acharya is revered as a descent of Mahavishnu, one with Sadashiva; hence the epithet "great lord" (maheshvara).
[^205-2]: Sri Rama Pandita (Ramai) is Srivasa's younger brother.
[^205-3]: Verses 20–27 expound jnana-yoga, the path of knowledge (cf. v. 28); after this the Lord proclaims devotion supreme (vv. 30–32).
[^205-4]: The opened palm and clenched fist depict the manifestation of the world and its withdrawal into the Lord.
[^205-5]: Literally, "from the taste of the totality" (samagri-rasa); the sense is unclear and the translation tentative.
[^205-6]: Cf. Bhagavata Purana 11.14.24, where Krishna likewise describes the devotee who purifies the world.

### Verse 26

*murāriḥ prāha bhagavannadhyātmaṁ na vidāmyaham|*

*Word for word:* murarih — Murari; praha — said; bhagavan — O Bhagavan; adhyatmam — adhyatma; na vidami — do not know; aham — I; tam — to him; praha — said; devah — the Lord; janasi — you know it; kamalakshat — from Kamalaksha; shrutam — heard; hi — for; tat — that.

**26.** Murari said: "O Bhagavan, I do not know the doctrine of the Self." The Lord replied to him: "You do — for you have heard it from Kamalaksha."[^206-6]

### Verse 27

इति सपदि निशम्य देववाक्यं प्रमुदितमनसो बभूवुरार्याः।

*iti sapadi niśamya devavākyaṁ pramuditamanaso babhūvurāryāḥ|*
*hariharapadapadmasīdhumattā nanṛturanimiṣā ivotsavāḍhyāḥ||27||*

*Word for word:* iti — thus; sapadi — at once; nishamya — hearing; deva-vakyam — the word of the Lord; pramudita-manasah — glad at heart; babhuvuh — became; aryah — the noble; hari-hara-pada-padma-sidhu-mattah — intoxicated with the wine of the lotus feet of Harihara; nanrituh — danced; animishah — the unblinking ones (gods); iva — like; utsava-adhyah — rich in festivity.

**27.** Hearing at once these words of the Lord, the noble ones rejoiced at heart and, intoxicated with the wine of the lotus feet of Harihara[^206-7], danced like the gods at a splendid festival.

*Thus ends the sixth sarga of the second prakrama of the poem "Sri Krishna-chaitanya-charitamrita."*

[^206-1]: Possibly the brahmana Gopala Chapala, struck with leprosy for offending Srivasa (his story is told in the Chaitanya-charitamrita, Adi 17).
[^206-2]: According to tradition, the Lord descended in answer to the prayers of Advaita Acharya.
[^206-3]: Kamalaksha is the worldly name of Advaita Acharya.
[^206-4]: Uddhava and Akrura are intimate devotees of Krishna.
[^206-5]: Sanskrit adhyatma: the doctrine of the Self and its identity with Brahman, as the Lord Himself had expounded it in 2.5.20–28.
[^206-6]: Cf. 2.4.22, where the Lord rebukes Murari for his song on the doctrine of the Self.
[^206-7]: Harihara: Hari and Hara (Vishnu and Shiva) in a single form; here, as in 2.7.6, apparently an epithet of Gaura. It may also be understood as "Hari (Gaura) and Hara (Advaita, revered as one with Sadashiva)."

## Prakrama 2, Sarga 7. Grace to the Devotees

*The appearance of the dancing Lord; the meaning of Srivasa's name; Murari's "Ramashtaka" and the name "Ramadasa"; service to Srivasa as worship of the Lord; Narayani receives the remnants of His meal*

### Verse 1

सितनवांशुकमस्तकवेष्टन-

वरभुजद्युतिरञ्जितकङ्कणः
स्फुटनवीनसरोजकरो बभौ॥१॥

*sitanavāṁśukamastakaveṣṭana-*
*staruṇavidrumasannibhahāradhṛk|*
*varabhujadyutirañjitakaṅkaṇaḥ*

*Word for word:* sita-nava-amshuka-mastaka-veshtanah — His head wrapped in new white cloth; taruna-vidruma-sannibha-hara-dhrik — wearing a necklace like young coral; vara-bhuja-dyuti-ranjita-kankanah — His bracelets tinted by the splendour of His fine arms; sphuta-navina-saroja-karah — His hands like freshly opened lotuses; babhau — shone.

**1.** His head was wrapped in new white cloth; He wore a necklace like young coral; His bracelets were tinted by the splendour of His fine arms, and His hands were like freshly opened lotuses — and He shone.

*Word for word:* chala-chela-nibaddha-dhati-dharah — wearing a loincloth bound with a fluttering cloth; aruna-bahir-vasanah — in a crimson outer garment; nata-vesha-dhrik — in a dancer's attire; vara-nitamba-vilambita-bahu — His arms hanging to His fine hips; vara-vilambi-naga-patih — (like) the lord of serpents; sphutam — plainly.

**2.** He wore a loincloth bound with a fluttering cloth, a crimson outer garment and a dancer's attire, and His arms, hanging down to His fine hips, plainly resembled the king of serpents[^207-1].

*padataladyutirañjitavidrumo*
*drutasuvarṇaruciḥ śanakairvrajan||3||*

*Word for word:* charana-pankaja-ranjita-nupurah — His anklets graced by His lotus feet; vara-nakha-dyuti-ranjita-shitaguh — the moon tinted by the splendour of His fine nails; pada-tala-dyuti-ranjita-vidrumah — coral tinted by the glow of His soles; druta-suvarna-ruchih — with the lustre of molten gold; shanakaih — slowly; vrajan — walking.

**3.** Anklets were graced by His lotus feet; the splendour of His lovely nails tinted the moon, the glow of His soles tinted coral; shining like molten gold, He moved with slow steps.

**12.** His neck is like a conch; the Unborn, His form is like a lotus; adorned with a string of pearls and a golden necklace, He shines like a rain-cloud with lightning and a flock of cranes. Rama, the teacher of the three worlds, I worship ever.

*Word for word:* iti — thus; sakala-nisham — the whole night; ninaya — spent; devah — the Lord; nija-jana-manasam — of the hearts of His own people; mude — for the joy; murarih — Murari; kshanam iva — as a moment; mahat-vatsarena — (a span) equal to a great year; mene — considered; anavaratam — unbroken; sukham — happiness; apuh — attained; arya-varyah — the best of the noble.

**27.** Thus the Lord Murari spent the whole night for the joy of the hearts of His own; a span as long as a great year He deemed a moment[^207-15] — and the best of the noble enjoyed unbroken happiness.

*Thus ends the seventh sarga, "Grace to the Devotees" (Bhakta-anugraha), of the second prakrama of the poem "Sri Krishna-chaitanya-charitamrita."*

[^207-1]: The text of this verse is partly damaged; the translation follows the general sense.
[^207-2]: Harihara: Hari and Hara (Vishnu and Shiva) in a single form; here an epithet of Gaura.
[^207-3]: Gopinatha is a brahmana of Navadvipa, a companion of the Lord.
[^207-4]: Verses 10–17 are the "Ramashtaka," the eight verses of Murari Gupta, a devotee of Rama.
[^207-5]: Brihaspati and Kavi (Shukra) are the planets Jupiter and Venus.
[^207-6]: The lotus is called "hundred-petalled" (shatapatra); Sita's five fingers appear as five more petals.
[^207-7]: Lakshmana is a descent of Shesha (Ananta), the serpent on whom Vishnu reclines.
[^207-8]: Rama protected the sacrifice of the sage Vishvamitra, a descendant of Kushika, from the rakshasas Maricha and Subahu.
[^207-9]: A pun: adushana means both "undefiled" and "without Dushana" (a rakshasa, Khara's brother). Trishiras and Kabandha are rakshasas of the Dandaka forest; Sugriva's enemy is Valin; the Ten-headed is Ravana.
[^207-10]: Pinaka is Shiva's bow; the lord of the Bhargavas is Parashurama; the father is King Dasharatha.
[^207-11]: Ramadasa means "servant of Rama."
[^207-12]: Murari addresses his listener, Damodara Pandita.
[^207-13]: Bhagavata Purana 11.14.20.
[^207-14]: Narayani, Srivasa's niece, later became the mother of Vrindavana Dasa Thakura, author of the Chaitanya-bhagavata.
[^207-15]: The sense of the line is unclear; the translation is tentative.

## Prakrama 2, Sarga 8. Grace to the Avadhuta

*The Lord sends His devotees for Nityananda; the meeting in the house of Nandana Acharya; the Lord honours Nityananda; in Srivasa's house He reveals to him His six-armed, four-armed and two-armed forms*

### Verse 1

ततः प्रभाते विमले नत्वा तं पुरुषर्षभम्।
गत्वा निजाश्रमं सर्वे स्नात्वा देवार्चनादिकम्॥१॥

*tataḥ prabhāte vimale natvā taṁ puruṣarṣabham|*
*gatvā nijāśramaṁ sarve snātvā devārcanādikam||1||*

*Word for word:* tatah — then; prabhate — at dawn; vimale — clear; natva — having bowed; tam — to Him; purusha-rishabham — the bull among men; gatva — having gone; nija-ashramam — to their own dwellings; sarve — all; snatva — having bathed; deva-archana-adikam — the worship of the Lord and the rest.

**1.** In the morning, when it grew light, all bowed to the Bull among men and went to their own dwellings; having bathed, worshipped the Lord and performed the other rites,

### Verse 2

कृत्वा भुक्त्वा यथान्यायमाजग्मुस्तत्पदाम्बुजम्।
तान्दृष्ट्वा हर्षसम्पूर्णो भगवान्मधुसूदनः॥२॥

*kṛtvā bhuktvā yathānyāyamājagmustatpadāmbujam|*
*tāndṛṣṭvā harṣasampūrṇo bhagavānmadhusūdanaḥ||2||*

*Word for word:* kritva — having performed; bhuktva — having eaten; yatha-nyayam — as was fitting; ajagmuh — came; tat-pada-ambujam — to His lotus feet; tan — them; drishtva — seeing; harsha-sampurnah — full of joy; bhagavan — Bhagavan; madhusudanah — Madhusudana.

**2.** and having eaten as was fitting, they came again to His lotus feet. Seeing them, Bhagavan Madhusudana was filled with joy

### Verse 3

ततः प्रोवाच भगवानवधूतः समागतः।
नित्यानन्द इति ख्यातो महात्मा तं समानय॥३॥

*tataḥ provāca bhagavānavadhūtaḥ samāgataḥ|*
*nityānanda iti khyāto mahātmā taṁ samānaya||3||*

*Word for word:* tatah — then; provacha — said; bhagavan — Bhagavan; avadhutah — the Avadhuta; samagatah — has arrived; nityanandah — Nityananda; iti — thus; khyatah — called; maha-atma — the great soul; tam — him; samanaya — bring.

**3.** and said: "The Avadhuta[^208-1] has come, a great soul named Nityananda. Bring him here.

### Verse 4

हे राम त्वं मुरारे च नारायणमुकुन्दकौ।
गच्छध्वं सत्वरा यूयं यत्रास्ते स महामतिः॥४॥

*he rāma tvaṁ murāre ca nārāyaṇamukundakau|*
*gacchadhvaṁ satvarā yūyaṁ yatrāste sa mahāmatiḥ||4||*

*Word for word:* he rama — O Rama; tvam — you; murare — O Murari; cha — and; narayana-mukundakau — Narayana and Mukunda; gachchhadhvam — go; satvarah — quickly; yuyam — you; yatra — where; aste — stays; sah — that; maha-matih — great-minded one.

**4.** Rama, and you, Murari, and Narayana and Mukunda[^208-2] — go quickly to where that great-minded one is staying."

### Verse 5

ततस्तदाज्ञया सर्वे दक्षिणे ग्रामसन्निधौ।
विचार्य तं न दृष्ट्वा ते समीयुस्तत्र सन्निधिम्॥५॥

[^208-1]: An avadhuta is a wandering renunciate who stands above outward rules; so the poem calls Nityananda.
[^208-2]: Rama is apparently Sri Rama Pandita, Srivasa's brother; Narayana is one of the Lord's companions in Navadvipa; Mukunda is Mukunda Datta.
[^208-3]: Nandana Acharya is a devotee of Navadvipa in whose house Nityananda stayed.
[^208-4]: The pastimes of Krishna and Balarama in Vrindavana; Nityananda is revered as Balarama. Before meeting the Lord he had wandered for many years among the holy places.
[^208-5]: The six-armed form (shadbhuja) unites the features of Rama, Krishna and Gaura Himself.
[^208-6]: The second line of the verse can also be understood as Nityananda's words to the Lord.
