## Prakrama 2, Sarga 9. The Acceptance of the Devotees' Worship

*The Lord sees the boy Krishna in a dream; Nityananda beholds the forms of Hari in Srivasa's house; messengers summon Advaita; Advaita comes, and the Lord accepts the worship of His devotees*

### Verse 1

श्रुत्वा कथामतितरां मुदितो महात्मा
दामोदरः पुनरुवाच मुरारिवैद्यम्।
अत्यद्भुतं वद विभोर्वपुषः स्वरूपं
स्वप्नेन दृष्टमपि यत्पुरुषोत्तमेन॥१॥

*śrutvā kathāmatitarāṁ mudito mahātmā*
*dāmodaraḥ punaruvāca murārivaidyam|*
*atyadbhutaṁ vada vibhorvapuṣaḥ svarūpaṁ*
*svapnena dṛṣṭamapi yatpuruṣottamena||1||*

*Word for word:* shrutva — having heard; katham — the narrative; atitaram — greatly; muditah — delighted; maha-atma — the great soul; damodarah — Damodara; punah — again; uvacha — said; murari-vaidyam — to Murari the physician; ati-adbhutam — most wondrous; vada — tell; vibhoh — of the all-powerful Lord; vapushah — of the body; sva-rupam — the true form; svapnena — in a dream; drishtam — seen; api — even; yat — which; purushottamena — by Purushottama.

**1.** Having heard this narrative, the great soul Damodara was overjoyed, and he spoke again to Murari the physician: "Tell me of the wondrous true form of the All-powerful One's body — the form which Purushottama[^209-1] beheld even in a dream."

### Verse 2

तं प्राह पुण्यचरितं स पुनर्मुरारिः
कृष्णस्य शुद्धमनसां महदुत्सवाय।
कृष्णस्वरूपमखिलाम्बरभूषणाढ्यं
स्वप्ने ददर्श पुनरेष नवीनकृष्णः॥२॥

*taṁ prāha puṇyacaritaṁ sa punarmurāriḥ*
*kṛṣṇasya śuddhamanasāṁ mahadutsavāya|*
*kṛṣṇasvarūpamakhilāmbarabhūṣaṇāḍhyaṁ*
*svapne dadarśa punareṣa navīnakṛṣṇaḥ||2||*

*Word for word:* tam — to him; praha — told; punya-charitam — the holy narrative; sah — he; punah — again; murarih — Murari; krishnasya — of Krishna; shuddha-manasam — of the pure-hearted; mahat-utsavaya — for the great festival; krishna-sva-rupam — the true form of Krishna; akhila-ambara-bhushana-adhyam — rich in every garment and ornament; svapne — in a dream; dadarsha — saw; punah — then; eshah — this; navina-krishnah — new Krishna.

**2.** And Murari again told him a holy tale of Krishna, a great festival for the pure in heart: "This new Krishna saw in a dream the true form of Krishna, richly arrayed in every garment and ornament.

### Verse 3

रात्रौ रुरोद भगवानतिविह्वलं सा
वीक्ष्यातिविस्मितमुखी तनयं बभाषे।
तात त्वमद्य किमलं स्वपरत्वमेषि
श्रुत्वा क्षणाद्धृतिमुवाह शचीं बभाषे॥३॥

*rātrau ruroda bhagavānativihvalaṁ sā*
*vīkṣyātivismitamukhī tanayaṁ babhāṣe|*
*tāta tvamadya kimalaṁ svaparatvameṣi*
*śrutvā kṣaṇāddhṛtimuvāha śacīṁ babhāṣe||3||*

*Word for word:* ratrau — at night; ruroda — wept; bhagavan — Bhagavan; ati-vihvalam — overwhelmed; sa — she; vikshya — seeing; ati-vismita-mukhi — her face full of wonder; tanayam — to her son; babhashe — said; tata — child; tvam — you; adya — today; kim — why; alam — so much; sva-paratvam — estrangement from yourself; eshi — do you reach; shrutva — hearing; kshanat — in a moment; dhritim — composure; uvaha — regained; shachim — to Shachi; babhashe — said.

**3.** In the night Bhagavan wept, utterly overcome. Seeing her son so, His mother, in great astonishment, said to Him: 'Child, why are You so beside Yourself today?' Hearing this, in a moment He regained His composure and said to Shachi:

### Verse 4

स्वप्ने मयाद्य नवनीरदतुल्यकान्ति-
र्मायूरपिच्छवरहाटककङ्कणाढ्यः।
बालो ललाटविलसत्कुटिलालकश्च
वंशीकरो रविकरोज्ज्वलपीतवस्त्रः॥४॥

*svapne mayādya navanīradatulyakānti-*
*rmāyūrapicchavarahāṭakakaṅkaṇāḍhyaḥ|*
*bālo lalāṭavilasatkuṭilālakaśca*
*vaṁśīkaro ravikarojjvalapītavastraḥ||4||*

*Word for word:* svapne — in a dream; maya — by Me; adya — today; nava-nirada-tulya-kantih — whose lustre was like a fresh rain-cloud; mayura-pichchha-vara-hataka-kankana-adhyah — adorned with a peacock feather and bracelets of fine gold; balah — a boy; lalata-vilasat-kutila-alakah — with curling locks playing on His forehead; cha — and; vamshi-karah — flute in hand; ravi-kara-ujjvala-pita-vastrah — in yellow garments bright as the sun's rays.

**4.** 'Today in a dream I saw a Boy whose lustre was like a fresh rain-cloud. He was adorned with a peacock feather and bracelets of pure gold, curling locks played upon His forehead, He held a flute in His hand, and His yellow garments shone like the rays of the sun.

### Verse 5

दृष्टोऽतिविह्वलतयाश्रुभिरावृताङ्गो
रोदिम्यनन्तरमनन्तसुखं ममाभूत्।
श्रुत्वा शचीसुतमुखाद्वचनामृतं सा
हर्षान्विता स्मितमुखी सुमुखी बभूव॥५॥

*dṛṣṭo'tivihvalatayāśrubhirāvṛtāṅgo*
*rodimyanantaramanantasukhaṁ mamābhūt|*
*śrutvā śacīsutamukhādvacanāmṛtaṁ sā*
*harṣānvitā smitamukhī sumukhī babhūva||5||*

*Word for word:* drishtah — was seen; ati-vihvalataya — from great agitation; ashrubhih — with tears; avrita-angah — My body covered; rodimi — I weep; anantaram — then; ananta-sukham — endless happiness; mama — to Me; abhut — came; shrutva — hearing; shachi-suta-mukhat — from the mouth of Shachi's son; vachana-amritam — the nectar of words; sa — she; harsha-anvita — filled with joy; smita-mukhi — smiling; su-mukhi — the fair-faced; babhuva — became.

**5.** When I saw Him I was so shaken that tears bathed My whole body; I weep — and then boundless happiness arose in Me.' Hearing these nectarean words from her son's lips, fair-faced Shachi was filled with joy and smiled.

### Verse 6

विश्वम्भरोऽतिपुलकावलिरञ्जिताङ्गः
प्रेमाश्रुवारिधिमुवाह विलोचनाभ्याम्।
कालेन तावदचिरेण समागतोऽसौ
श्रीवासवेश्मनि शुभे शुशुभेऽवधूतः॥६॥

*viśvambharo'tipulakāvalirañjitāṅgaḥ*
*premāśruvāridhimuvāha vilocanābhyām|*
*kālena tāvadacireṇa samāgato'sau*
*śrīvāsaveśmani śubhe śuśubhe'vadhūtaḥ||6||*

*Word for word:* vishvambharah — Vishvambhara; ati-pulaka-avali-ranjita-angah — His body adorned with thick rows of bristling hair; prema-ashru-varidhim — an ocean of tears of love; uvaha — poured forth; vilochanabhyam — from His two eyes; kalena — in time; tavat — meanwhile; achirena — soon; samagatah — having come; asau — he; shrivasa-veshmani — in the house of Srivasa; shubhe — auspicious; shushubhe — shone; avadhutah — the Avadhuta.

**6.** And Vishvambhara, His whole body adorned with thick rows of bristling hair, poured an ocean of tears of love from His eyes. Meanwhile, before long, the Avadhuta arrived and shone in the blessed house of Srivasa.

### Verse 7

तत्रैव सर्वभुवनैकसुखाभिलाषी
प्रेमाश्रुपूर्णवदनः शुशुभेऽवधूतः।
दृष्ट्वा हरेरतितरां भुवि दुर्लभाङ्गं
तेजोमयं कमलनेत्रमुदारवेशम्॥७॥

*tatraiva sarvabhuvanaikasukhābhilāṣī*
*premāśrupūrṇavadanaḥ śuśubhe'vadhūtaḥ|*
*dṛṣṭvā hareratitarāṁ bhuvi durlabhāṅgaṁ*
*tejomayaṁ kamalanetramudāraveśam||7||*

*Word for word:* tatra eva — right there; sarva-bhuvana-eka-sukha-abhilashi — desiring only the happiness of all the worlds; prema-ashru-purna-vadanah — his face full of tears of love; shushubhe — shone; avadhutah — the Avadhuta; drishtva — seeing; hareh — of Hari; atitaram — exceedingly; bhuvi — on earth; durlabha-angam — the form hard to attain; tejah-mayam — made of radiance; kamala-netram — lotus-eyed; udara-vesham — splendidly attired.

**7.** There the Avadhuta shone, desiring one thing only — the happiness of all the worlds, his face streaming with tears of love. He beheld a form of Hari hardly to be attained on earth — radiant, lotus-eyed, splendidly attired:

### Verse 8

कक्षे गदावररथाङ्गदरं दधानं

**8.** on one side He held the fine club, the discus and the conch, on the left the lovely flute, the excellent bow Sharnga[^209-2] and the thousand-petalled lotus; He glowed like molten gold, He was adorned with the splendid Kaustubha, and divine makara earrings gleamed upon His cheeks;

### Verse 9

**9.** a wondrous jewel shone on His brow, on His lovely neck lay an ornament of blue lotuses and a necklace of emerald beads, He was resplendent with a white necklace set in silver, and His garments were golden as the rays of the sun. Seeing this, the Avadhuta was beside himself.

### Verse 10

दृष्ट्वा पुनर्मुरलिकावरणाङ्गहीनं

लोकानुरूपचरितं च ततो जहास॥१०॥

*Word for word:* drishtva — seeing; punah — next; muralika-varana-anga-hinam — without the arms that clasped the flute; rupam — the form; tatha eva — the very same; vara-bahu-chatushtayam — with four splendid arms; sah — he; harsha-aplutah — flooded with joy; kshanam — for a moment; atha — then; dvi-bhujam — the two-armed One; dadarsha — saw; loka-anurupa-charitam — whose deeds befit the world of men; cha — and; tatah — then; jahasa — laughed.

**10.** Next he saw the same form, now without the arms that clasped the flute[^209-3] — with four splendid arms; and, flooded with joy, a moment later he saw Him two-armed, in the form whose deeds befit the world of men — and then he laughed.

### Verse 11

एवं हरेरतितरां दिवि दुर्लभं य-

*Word for word:* evam — thus; hareh — of Hari; atitaram — exceedingly; divi — in heaven; durlabham — hard to attain; yat — which; drishtva — having seen; sva-rupam — the true form; achirena — at once; nanarta — danced; sah — he; api — too; alingya — embracing; tatra — there; sva-janan — his own people; nava-toya-rashau — in an ocean of fresh waters; magnah — immersed; babhuva — became; nitaram — wholly; avadhuta-devah — the divine Avadhuta.

**11.** Having thus seen the true form of Hari, which is hard to attain even in heaven, the divine Avadhuta at once broke into dance; embracing his own people there, he sank wholly into an ocean of fresh waters.

**12.** Glory to Krishna's elder brother[^209-4], filled with the rasa of Gaura! Peals of laughter grace his cheeks, his eyes are lovely with the intoxication of varuni; clad in blue, he bears the pestle, the plough and the staff.

**13.** The Lord said to Srivasa and Rama, to Murari the physician and to Narayana: "Go to Advaita's house and let the best of brahmanas know: this Avadhuta will come to him."[^209-5]

**14.** Hearing these words of Hari, they went joyfully to Advaita's lotus feet; arriving on the blessed bank of the heavenly river[^209-6], they bowed to him and conveyed Hari's infinitely holy command.

**15.** Hearing of the Lord's wondrous, brilliant power, the Acharya rejoiced, sang and danced; and again and again he sank into the great ocean of bliss and rose to its surface.

*Word for word:* sthitva — having stayed; tatah — then; tatra — there; dina-dvayam — two days; te — they; dhyatva — meditating; pada-abjam — on the lotus feet; sva-griham — to home; samiyuh — came; acharya-mukhyah — led by the Acharya; cha — and; hareh — of Hari; pada-abje — at the lotus feet; nivedya — having reported; sarvam — everything; sahasa — at once; nananduh — rejoiced.

**16.** Having stayed there two days, they returned home, meditating on His lotus feet; and, led by the Acharya, they reported everything at Hari's lotus feet and at once were filled with joy.

**17.** Having come there, the Acharya at an auspicious time beheld Him whose eyes are lotus petals. Seeing His face, he let out a lion's roar and drew near to Mukunda, who takes away the sorrows of those who surrender to Him.

*Word for word:* agatya — having come; gehe — home; dvija-varya-sattamah — the best of excellent brahmanas; bhishak-tama-adyah — headed by the best of physicians; hari-nama-bhashanah — uttering the name of Hari; stribhyah — to the women; cha — and; sarve — all; jagaduh — told; muda-anvitah — full of joy; hareh — of Hari; charitram — the deeds; nikhilam — all; jagat-guroh — of the Teacher of the world.

**23.** those best of excellent brahmanas, led by the best of physicians[^209-8], came home uttering the name of Hari, and all of them joyfully told their wives the whole story of Hari, the Teacher of the world.

*Thus ends the ninth sarga, "The Acceptance of the Devotees' Worship" (Bhakta-puja-upagrahana), of the second prakrama of the poem "Sri Krishna-chaitanya-charitamrita."*

[^209-1]: Purushottama ("the Highest of persons") here is Lord Gaura Himself; Damodara asks to hear of the vision He Himself had in a dream (vv. 2–5).
[^209-2]: Sharnga is Vishnu's bow. These six attributes point to the six-armed form spoken of in the previous sarga.
[^209-3]: The reading is conjectural: the arms that held the flute vanish, and the four-armed form remains.
[^209-4]: Krishna's elder brother is Balarama, who appeared as Nityananda; the blue garments, the plough and the pestle are his marks, and the intoxication of varuni (wine) is an image of his rapture in love.
[^209-5]: The syntax of the second half of the verse is unclear; another reading is possible: "Go to Advaita's house — this Avadhuta too will go, to inform the best of brahmanas." Rama is Sri Rama Pandita, Srivasa's brother; Narayana is a companion of the Lord in Navadvipa.
[^209-6]: The heavenly river is the Ganga; on its bank, at Shantipura, lived Advaita.
[^209-7]: Kaivalya is liberation as merging into Brahman, which to devotees is a trifle beside love for the Lord.
[^209-8]: Apparently Murari Gupta himself, a physician by calling.

## Prakrama 2, Sarga 10. The Pastimes of Dance

*The Lord honours Haridasa and sends Advaita home; the shreds of Nityananda's kaupina; the Lord carries Srivasa away and reappears; pastimes in the mood of the gopis; the washing of the Avadhuta's feet; Haridasa and Advaita come*

### Verse 1

स्नात्वा द्युनद्यां जगदीशपूजां
कृत्वा समीयुः पुनरेव सन्निधौ।
विश्वम्भरस्याम्बुजलोचनस्य
सोऽपि प्रमोदेन ददर्श तान्प्रभुः॥१॥

*snātvā dyunadyāṁ jagadīśapūjāṁ*

*viśvambharasyāmbujalocanasya*
*so'pi pramodena dadarśa tānprabhuḥ||1||*

*Word for word:* snatva — having bathed; dyunadyam — in the heavenly river; jagat-isha-pujam — the worship of the Lord of the world; kritva — having performed; samiyuh — came; punah eva — once again; sannidhau — into the presence; vishvambharasya — of Vishvambhara; ambuja-lochanasya — the lotus-eyed; sah — He; api — too; pramodena — with delight; dadarsha — saw; tan — them; prabhuh — the Lord.

**1.** Having bathed in the heavenly river and worshipped the Lord of the world, they came once more into the presence of lotus-eyed Vishvambhara; and the Lord too looked upon them with delight.

**13.** The great souls searched but did not find Him. Knowing that they were troubled, the Unborn, who delights in His own free will, Himself appeared before them, and they eagerly crowded round Him on every side.

**14.** And each of them, looking with entire devotion, gained through the nature of the gopis, upon Krishna, the Lord with the forest garland, prayed: "May the Great Lord show me grace, so that this Bhagavan may become my beloved!"

### Verse 15

**15.** For here is Sri Krishna Himself, full of rasa and wholly intent on awakening the feeling of the cowherd women. Perceiving in the devotees who bowed before Him the feeling of the gopis, He performs the pastime of stealing the garments[^210-4] and other pastimes.

### Verse 16

**16.** And so once, at nightfall, the Holder of the discus — the knower of rasa, the giver of rasa to men — pulled the garments off His servants with His two lotus hands and left them naked.

**17.** Having played this game, in a moment the Lord gave back all their garments; and they gladly put them on again and made merry together with Murari[^210-5].

### Verse 18

गायन्हरेर्नाम पुनर्ननर्त

**18.** Singing the name of Hari, He danced again with them, pure of heart — the Lord of playful gait, whose lustre of molten gold destroys the impurity of the world.

### Verse 19

**19.** Then the Avadhuta came again and, happy, made merry; at once he broke into dance and sang of Hari's qualities. As once the cowherd boys played with Krishna and the Plough-bearer[^210-6], so here too did the Lotus-eyed One.

### Verse 20

**20.** When the dancing was over, Bhagavan said to the foremost brahmanas: "Wash the Avadhuta's feet and take that water." And they reverently carried out His command.

### Verse 21

**21.** Having drunk the water of his feet, they, filled with rasa, joyfully dance and sing and cry aloud together with Sri Gaurachandra; and the Avadhuta, laughing, fell to the ground.

### Verse 22

**22.** And then He[^210-7] rejoiced, dispelling the dire sorrow of men's hearts with the nectarean flood of His speech, with His gait, His laughter and the glances of the Lotus-eyed One.

### Verse 23

**23.** Knowing that He was sporting thus, the Thirty[^210-8], standing in the sky, bowed to Him in His beautiful attire; greatly amazed, filled with songs of praise, the immortals extolled Him and gazed upon Him in delight.

**24.** There came the excellent Sri Haridasa: on his breast shone a crystal jewel like a moon, his feet were adorned with lovely anklets; and the sage danced beside the Lord.

**25.** The wise and excellent Advaita came again. Hari, the Lord who loves His devotees, Himself worshipped him with water for the feet, arghya, scents, unbroken rice, sandal and the rest, and then gave him His bidding.

### Verse 26

ससम्भ्रमेणादरतो गृहीत्वा

**26.** With reverent awe and respect accepting and eating, with a loud roar, that supremely great prasada, the best of acharyas, whose renown is wide, made merry with Hari in a great festival.

शृणोति यः कृष्णकथामिमां शुभां

लभेत पाण्डित्यमखण्डितं च
देहावसाने च हरेः पुरं व्रजेत्॥२७॥

*śṛṇoti yaḥ kṛṣṇakathāmimāṁ śubhāṁ*
*premānvitaḥ syātsa tu śuddhabhāvam|*
*labheta pāṇḍityamakhaṇḍitaṁ ca*

*Word for word:* shrinoti — hears; yah — who; krishna-katham — the narrative of Krishna; imam — this; shubham — auspicious; prema-anvitah — full of love; syat — will become; sah — he; tu — indeed; shuddha-bhavam — pure feeling; labheta — will obtain; pandityam — learning; akhanditam — unimpaired; cha — and; deha-avasane — at the end of the body; cha — and; hareh — of Hari; puram — to the abode; vrajet — will go.

**27.** Whoever hears this auspicious narrative of Krishna will be filled with love, will gain pure feeling and unimpaired learning, and at the end of the body will go to the abode of Hari.

*Thus ends the tenth sarga, "The Pastimes of Dance" (Nritya-vilasa), of the second prakrama of the poem "Sri Krishna-chaitanya-charitamrita."*

[^210-1]: Haridasa is Haridasa Thakura, the great devotee of the holy name.
[^210-2]: The four kinds of food are those that are chewed, sucked, licked and drunk.
[^210-3]: A kaupina is a renunciate's loincloth. The Lord gave the shreds of Nityananda's kaupina to the devotees as a sacred relic.
[^210-4]: The stealing of the garments is Krishna's pastime in Vrindavana, when He carried off the clothes of the bathing gopis; here the Lord repeats it with devotees in whom the feeling of the gopis has awakened.
[^210-5]: "Murari" ("Enemy of Mura") is here apparently an epithet of the Lord; it may also be understood as "together with Murari Gupta."
[^210-6]: The Plough-bearer is Balarama. Nityananda (Balarama) and Gaura (Krishna) play with the devotees as once with the cowherd boys of Vrindavana.
[^210-7]: The Lord; it may also be understood that Nityananda rejoiced in the speech, gait, laughter and glances of the Lotus-eyed One.
[^210-8]: The Thirty (tridasha) are the gods, conventionally thirty-three in number.

## Prakrama 2, Sarga 11. The Plunge into the Jahnavi

*The brahmana Vanamali sees the boy Krishna; the Lord in the mood of Nrisimha; the Lord as Shiva on a singer's shoulders; a brahmana woman takes the dust of His feet, and the Lord throws Himself into the Ganga*

### Verse 1

भिक्षुः कश्चिद्वनमाली द्विजस्तत्र समागतः।
सपुत्रो देवदेवेशं ददर्श च ननर्त च॥१॥

*bhikṣuḥ kaścidvanamālī dvijastatra samāgataḥ|*
*saputro devadeveśaṁ dadarśa ca nanarta ca||1||*

*Word for word:* bhikshuh — a mendicant; kashchit — certain; vanamali — Vanamali; dvijah — a brahmana; tatra — there; samagatah — came; sa-putrah — with his son; deva-deva-isham — the Lord of the god of gods; dadarsha — saw; cha — and; nanarta — danced; cha — and.

**1.** Once a certain mendicant brahmana named Vanamali came there with his son; he saw the Lord of the god of gods and broke into dance.

### Verse 2

तं दृष्ट्वा भगवान्प्रीत्या तेन सार्धं हरिं जगौ।
हरेः सोऽपि प्रसादेन सपुत्रो मुमुदे सुखम्॥२॥

*taṁ dṛṣṭvā bhagavānprītyā tena sārdhaṁ hariṁ jagau|*
*hareḥ so'pi prasādena saputro mumude sukham||2||*

*Word for word:* tam — him; drishtva — seeing; bhagavan — Bhagavan; pritya — lovingly; tena — with him; sardham — together; harim — of Hari; jagau — sang; hareh — of Hari; sah — he; api — too; prasadena — by the grace; sa-putrah — with his son; mumude — rejoiced; sukham — happily.

**2.** Seeing him, Bhagavan lovingly sang of Hari together with him; and he and his son rejoiced happily by the grace of Hari.

### Verse 3

एकदा कीर्तनपरे हरौ नृत्यति स द्विजः।
ददर्श बालकं कञ्चिच्छ्यामं पीताम्बरावृतम्॥३॥

*ekadā kīrtanapare harau nṛtyati sa dvijaḥ|*
*dadarśa bālakaṁ kañcicchyāmaṁ pītāmbarāvṛtam||3||*

*Word for word:* ekada — once; kirtana-pare — absorbed in kirtana; harau — while Hari; nrityati — is dancing; sah — that; dvijah — brahmana; dadarsha — saw; balakam — a boy; kanchit — certain; shyamam — dark; pita-ambara-avritam — clad in yellow garments.

**3.** Once, while Hari was dancing, absorbed in kirtana, that brahmana saw a certain dark boy clad in yellow garments.

### Verse 4

दृष्टो दृष्टो मया देव इति हृष्टो बभूव ह।
स जन्म सार्थकं मेने भिक्षुधर्मो द्विजोत्तमः॥४॥

*dṛṣṭo dṛṣṭo mayā deva iti hṛṣṭo babhūva ha|*
*sa janma sārthakaṁ mene bhikṣudharmo dvijottamaḥ||4||*

*Word for word:* drishtah drishtah — seen, seen; maya — by me; devah — the Lord; iti — thus; hrishtah — jubilant; babhuva — became; ha — indeed; sah — that; janma — birth; sa-arthakam — fulfilled; mene — considered; bhikshu-dharmah — following the mendicant's way; dvija-uttamah — the best of brahmanas.

**4.** "I have seen the Lord, I have seen Him!" he cried, jubilant; and that best of brahmanas, who lived as a mendicant, held that his birth had attained its purpose.

### Verse 5

पुत्रं गृहीत्वा हस्ताभ्यामागतः प्रभुसन्निधिम्।
एवं भिक्षुः स हृष्टाङ्गः पुलकावलिमुद्वहन्॥५॥

*putraṁ gṛhītvā hastābhyāmāgataḥ prabhusannidhim|*

[^211-1]: The Vishnu-sahasranama ("Thousand Names of Vishnu") from the Mahabharata or a similar hymn recited at rites.
[^211-2]: Nrisimha (Narasimha, Nrihari) is the Man-lion, the incarnation of Vishnu who tore apart the demon Hiranyakashipu for the sake of His devotee Prahlada.
[^211-3]: The singer on whose shoulders the Lord sits is likened to Nandin, the bull on which Shiva rides.
[^211-4]: Hara is Shiva. The horn, the damaru drum and the matted locks are his marks; Shiva is the greatest devotee of Rama, ever repeating His name.
[^211-5]: The Shiva-mahimna-stotra ("Hymn on the Greatness of Shiva"), ascribed to Pushpadanta. Mukunda is Mukunda Datta, the singer among the Lord's companions.
[^211-6]: Taking the dust of someone's feet is a sign of worship, as before the Lord or a saint. The Lord, playing the part of a devotee, held Himself unworthy of such honour, and the woman's deed filled Him with remorse.

## Prakrama 2, Sarga 12. The Great Manifestation and the Ablution

*The Lord returns from the northern bank of the Ganga; Murari consoles Him; the Lord reveals His great majesty, and the devotees bathe and worship Him*

### Verse 1

*tato vāṭyāṁ murāreste jhaṭityāgatya seśvarāḥ|*

**1.** Then together with the Lord they hurried to Murari's house; having sat there a little while, they went on to the dwelling of Vijaya[^212-1].

### Verse 2

*uṣitvā rajanīṁ tatra prabhāte bhagavānparaḥ|*
*jagāmottarakaṁ kūlaṁ sa jāhnavyā bhramaddrutam||2||*

*Word for word:* ushitva — having spent; rajanim — the night; tatra — there; prabhate — at dawn; bhagavan — Bhagavan; parah — the Supreme; jagama — went; uttarakam — northern; kulam — to the bank; sah — He; jahnavyah — of the Jahnavi; bhraman — wandering; drutam — swiftly.

**2.** Having spent the night there, at dawn the Supreme Bhagavan went to the northern bank of the Jahnavi and roamed swiftly about.

### Verse 3

ब्राह्मणाः साधवः शान्ता विनयेन द्विजोत्तमाः।

*brāhmaṇāḥ sādhavaḥ śāntā vinayena dvijottamāḥ|*

### Verse 4

## Prakrama 2, Sarga 13. The Brahmana's Curse as a Boon

[^213-2]: Jagannatha and Madhava are the brothers Jagai and Madhai, notorious sinners of Navadvipa, later delivered by the Lord and Nityananda.

## Prakrama 2, Sarga 14. Absorption in Balabhadra

*The Lord takes on the mood of Balarama: He calls for honey-wine, dances as if drunk, sees Halayudha and displays His form; the devotees see Balarama's companions and His golden club*

### Verse 1

अथ प्रभाते विमले द्युनाथे

स पाठयन्दैवतगौरचन्द्रो
बभूव नीलाम्बरभावभावितः॥१॥

*atha prabhāte vimale dyunāthe*
*smaranmunibrāhmaṇasajjanānbahūn|*
*sa pāṭhayandaivatagauracandro*
*babhūva nīlāmbarabhāvabhāvitaḥ||1||*

*Word for word:* atha — then; prabhate — at dawn; vimale — clear; dyu-nathe — (when) the lord of the sky (the sun); smaran — remembering; muni-brahmana-sat-janan — sages, brahmanas and saintly people; bahun — many; sah — He; pathayan — teaching (pupils); daivata-gaurachandrah — the divine Gaurachandra; babhuva — became; nila-ambara-bhava-bhavitah — imbued with the mood of Nilambara (the Blue-clad, Balarama).

**1.** One morning at dawn, when the sun shone clear in the sky, the divine Gaurachandra, while teaching His pupils and remembering many sages, brahmanas and saintly people, became imbued with the mood of Nilambara[^214-1].

*Word for word:* sah — He; hasayan — making (all) laugh; dehi — give; madhuni — honey; sampratam — now; tu — and; ativa — exceedingly; tam — that; megha-samam — like a thundercloud; svanam — sound; punah — again; shushrava — heard; tasmin samaye — at that moment; halayudham — Halayudha (the Plough-armed); nila-ambaram — blue-clad; shveta-mahidharam — a white mountain; prabhum — the Lord.

## Prakrama 2, Sarga 15. Description of the Gopis' Mood — Bhakti-yoga

*The Lord speaks of His vision of Varaha and Halayudha and asks for His flute; in Chandrashekhara's house a play is staged: the Lord in women's dress, Srivasa as Narada, Gadadhara as a gopi; Narada speaks of the greatness of devotion*

*Thus ends the fifteenth sarga, "Description of the Gopis' Mood — Bhakti-yoga" (Gopi-bhava-varnana — Bhakti-yoga), of the second prakrama of the poem "Sri Krishna-chaitanya-charitamrita."*

[^215-1]: Varaha is the incarnation of Vishnu as a boar who raised the Earth from the waters; "He whose body is sacrifice" is His standing epithet.
[^215-2]: The mood of Balarama (see sarga 2.14) gives way to the mood of Krishna with His flute.
[^215-3]: Bhishmaka's daughter is Rukmini, Krishna's consort; here the name refers to the Lord's wife (Vishnupriya).
[^215-4]: The play at the house of Chandrashekhara Acharya, in which the Lord took a woman's role and His companions played other parts, is also described at length in other lives of the Lord.
[^215-5]: Shripati's elder brother is Srivasa.
[^215-6]: Narada (Srivasa) reminds Gadadhara, who is playing a gopi, of her former birth as an apsara.
[^215-7]: Bhagavata Purana 10.47.63 — Uddhava's words about the gopis of Vraja.
[^215-8]: Bhagavata Purana, canto 6, chapters 1–2: dying, the sinful Ajamila called out to his son named Narayana; the messengers of Yama withdrew, and he was saved.
[^215-9]: The verse is obscure; the reading and interpretation are conjectural.

## Prakrama 2, Sarga 16. The Manifestation of All Energies

*The play in Chandrashekhara's house continues: Haridasa, Advaita and Nityananda enter; the Lord appears as a gopi, then in the mood of Kamala and of the Goddess, displays all power, feeds the devotees with milk and in the morning returns home*

### Verse 1

प्राविशत्तदनु दण्डधरोऽग्रतः
पूर्णचन्द्रसदृशो हरिदासः।
कीर्तनं कुरु हरेरिति वादी
बोधयंस्त्रिजगतीं परितप्ताम्॥१॥

*prāviśattadanu daṇḍadharo'grataḥ*
*pūrṇacandrasadṛśo haridāsaḥ|*
*kīrtanaṁ kuru hareriti vādī*
*bodhayaṁstrijagatīṁ paritaptām||1||*

*Word for word:* pravishat — entered; tat-anu — then; danda-dharah — bearing a staff; agratah — first; purna-chandra-sadrishah — like the full moon; haridasah — Haridasa; kirtanam — kirtana; kuru — perform; hareh — of Hari; iti — thus; vadi — saying; bodhayan — awakening; tri-jagatim — the three worlds; paritaptam — burning (with suffering).

**1.** Then Haridasa, like the full moon, entered first, a staff in his hand[^216-1]. "Sing the kirtana of Hari!" he proclaimed, awakening the three worlds, which burn with suffering.

*vaiṣṇavā nanṛturudgatanetra-*
*vāribhistimitavigrahabhājaḥ||2||*

*Word for word:* tasya — his; tat — those; vachanam — words; abja-mukhasya — of the lotus-faced one; sannipiya — drinking in; hrishita-anga-ruhah — their hair bristling with joy; te — those; vaishnavah — Vaishnavas; nanrituh — danced; udgata-netra-varibhih — with tears welling from their eyes; stimita-vigraha-bhajah — their bodies drenched.

**2.** Drinking in those words of the lotus-faced Haridasa, the Vaishnavas danced; their hair bristled with joy, and their bodies were drenched with the tears that welled from their eyes.

**4.** The excellent Advaita, born of a portion of the Lord[^216-2], moist with the rasa of Hari's feet, danced together with the other followers like a maddened lion, untamable within.

*Thus ends the sixteenth sarga, "The Manifestation of All Energies" (Sarva-shakti-prakasha), of the second prakrama of the poem "Sri Krishna-chaitanya-charitamrita."*

[^216-2]: Advaita Acharya is revered as the incarnation of a portion of Mahavishnu.
[^216-3]: Baladeva is Nityananda.
[^216-4]: Vasudeva is a name of Krishna. The compound may also be understood as "in a special attire prepared by Vasudeva."
[^216-5]: The breeze from the Malaya hills in South India, where sandalwood grows, is famed in poetry for its coolness and fragrance.
[^216-6]: Kamala is Lakshmi, the Lord's eternal consort.
[^216-7]: The Goddess (Bhagavati) is the original energy of the Lord, possessing all powers.
[^216-8]: Chandi is the fierce Goddess (Durga). The Lord jokes: people will take those devoted to Him in the form of the Goddess for Shaktas, votaries of Chandi.

## Prakrama 2, Sarga 17. The Admonition of Sri Murari Gupta

*For a week the Lord's wondrous radiance lingers; Srivasa asks about the dharma of the ages, and the Lord speaks of the holy name; the Lord longs to leave for Mathura, and Murari holds Him back*

### Verse 1

श्रीचन्द्रशेखराचार्यरत्नवाट्यां महाप्रभुः।
ननर्त यत्र तत्रासीत्तेजस्तत्त्ववदद्भुतम्॥१॥

*śrīcandraśekharācāryaratnavāṭyāṁ mahāprabhuḥ|*
*nanarta yatra tatrāsīttejastattvavadadbhutam||1||*

*Word for word:* shri-chandrashekhara-acharyaratna-vatyam — in the homestead of Sri Chandrashekhara Acharyaratna; maha-prabhuh — Mahaprabhu; nanarta — danced; yatra — where; tatra — there; asit — there was; tejah — a radiance; tattva-vat — in very truth; adbhutam — wondrous.

**1.** In the homestead of Sri Chandrashekhara Acharyaratna[^217-1], where Mahaprabhu had danced, a radiance shone forth — wondrous in very truth.

### Verse 2

सप्ताहं शीतलं चन्द्रतेजसा सदृशं हरेः।
चञ्चलेव सुदुष्प्रेक्ष्यं चित्ताह्लादकरं शुचि॥२॥

*saptāhaṁ śītalaṁ candratejasā sadṛśaṁ hareḥ|*
*cañcaleva suduṣprekṣyaṁ cittāhlādakaraṁ śuci||2||*

*Word for word:* sapta-aham — for seven days; shitalam — cool; chandra-tejasa — to the light of the moon; sadrisham — similar; hareh — of Hari; chanchala — lightning; iva — like; su-dushprekshyam — very hard to look at; chitta-ahlada-karam — gladdening the heart; shuchi — pure.

**2.** For seven days Hari's radiance was cool like moonlight, yet dazzling to the eyes like lightning — pure and gladdening to the heart.

### Verse 3

ये ये तत्रागता लोका ऊचुस्तत्र कथं दृशोः।
उन्मीलने न शक्ताः स्म विद्युद्वत्प्रेक्ष्य भूतले॥३॥

*ye ye tatrāgatā lokā ūcustatra kathaṁ dṛśoḥ|*
*unmīlane na śaktāḥ sma vidyudvatprekṣya bhūtale||3||*

*Word for word:* ye ye — all who; tatra — there; agatah — came; lokah — people; uchuh — said; tatra — there; katham — how is it; drishoh — of the eyes; unmilane — to the opening; na shaktah sma — we are not able; vidyut-vat — something like lightning; prekshya — seeing; bhu-tale — on the earth.

**3.** All who came there said, "How is it that we cannot open our eyes? It is as if we were seeing lightning on the earth!"

### Verse 4

तच्छ्रुत्वा वैष्णवाः सर्वे हर्षादूचुर्न किञ्चन।
जानन्तोऽपि महाभागा बहिर्मुखजनान्प्रति॥४॥

*tacchrutvā vaiṣṇavāḥ sarve harṣādūcurna kiñcana|*
*jānanto'pi mahābhāgā bahirmukhajanānprati||4||*

*Word for word:* tat — that; shrutva — hearing; vaishnavah — the Vaishnavas; sarve — all; harshat — out of joy; uchuh na kinchana — said nothing; janantah — knowing; api — though; maha-bhagah — the greatly fortunate; bahir-mukha-janan prati — to the people turned away (from God).

**4.** Hearing this, the Vaishnavas, out of joy, said nothing: those greatly fortunate souls knew the truth of it, but did not reveal it to people turned away from God.

### Verse 5

अथ पप्रच्छ श्रीवासो भगवन्तं जगद्गुरुम्।
कलावेव हरेर्नामकीर्तनं समुदाहृतम्॥५॥

*atha papraccha śrīvāso bhagavantaṁ jagadgurum|*
*kalāveva harernāmakīrtanaṁ samudāhṛtam||5||*

*Word for word:* atha — then; paprachchha — asked; shrivasah — Srivasa; bhagavantam — Bhagavan; jagat-gurum — the teacher of the world; kalau eva — for Kali alone; hareh — of Hari; nama-kirtanam — the chanting of the name; samudahritam — is declared.

**5.** Then Srivasa asked Bhagavan, the teacher of the world, "The chanting of Hari's name is declared for the age of Kali alone.

### Verse 6

किं सत्यादियुगस्यास्ति फलं न्यूनं कथञ्चन।
तच्छ्रुत्वा भगवान्प्राह श्रूयतां कथयामि ते॥६॥

*kiṁ satyādiyugasyāsti phalaṁ nyūnaṁ kathañcana|*
*tacchrutvā bhagavānprāha śrūyatāṁ kathayāmi te||6||*

*Word for word:* kim — is it that; satya-adi-yugasya — of Satya and the other ages; asti — is; phalam — the fruit; nyunam — lesser; kathanchana — in any way; tat — that; shrutva — hearing; bhagavan — Bhagavan; praha — said; shruyatam — listen; kathayami — I shall tell; te — you.

**6.** Is the fruit of the Satya age and the others, then, in any way less?[^217-2]" Hearing this, Bhagavan replied, "Listen, and I shall tell you.

### Verse 7

सत्ये धर्मस्य पूर्णत्वाद्ध्यानेनैवोपसाध्यते।
तत्फलं यज्ञमात्रेण त्रेतायां द्वापरे युगे॥७॥

*satye dharmasya pūrṇatvāddhyānenaivopasādhyate|*
*tatphalaṁ yajñamātreṇa tretāyāṁ dvāpare yuge||7||*

*Word for word:* satye — in the Satya age; dharmasya — of dharma; purnatvat — because of the fullness; dhyanena eva — by meditation alone; upasadhyate — is attained; tat-phalam — that fruit; yajna-matrena — by sacrifice alone; tretayam — in the Treta age; dvapare yuge — in the Dvapara age.

**7.** In the Satya age, when dharma is whole, the fruit is attained by meditation alone; in the Treta age the same fruit comes by sacrifice alone; in the Dvapara age,

### Verse 8

पूजनेन कलौ पापैर्न शक्तास्ते हरिः स्वयम्।
नामस्वरूपो भगवानागत्य शुशुभे प्रभुः॥८॥

*pūjanena kalau pāpairna śaktāste hariḥ svayam|*
*nāmasvarūpo bhagavānāgatya śuśubhe prabhuḥ||8||*

*Word for word:* pujanena — by worship (in Dvapara); kalau — in Kali; papaih — because of sins; na shaktah — not capable; te — they (people); harih — Hari; svayam — Himself; nama-svarupah — in the form of the name; bhagavan — Bhagavan; agatya — having come; shushubhe — shone forth; prabhuh — the Lord.

**8.** by worship. But in Kali people, because of their sins, are capable of none of these; and so Hari Himself, Bhagavan, the Lord, has come in the form of the name and shone forth[^217-3].

### Verse 9

कृतादिषु त्रयः शक्त्या ध्यानयज्ञार्चनादयः।
दारुणे च कलौ पापे स्वयमेवानुपद्यते॥९॥

*kṛtādiṣu trayaḥ śaktyā dhyānayajñārcanādayaḥ|*
*dāruṇe ca kalau pāpe svayamevānupadyate||9||*

*Word for word:* krita-adishu — in Krita and the other (ages); trayah — the three (ways); shaktya — by (human) capacity; dhyana-yajna-archana-adayah — meditation, sacrifice, worship and the rest; darune — in the terrible; cha — but; kalau — Kali; pape — sinful; svayam eva — He Himself; anupadyate — comes.

**9.** In Krita and the ages that follow, the three ways — meditation, sacrifice, worship and the rest — are carried out by human strength; but in the terrible, sinful age of Kali He comes Himself."

### Verse 10

तच्छ्रुत्वा हर्षितो विप्रः श्रीवासः पण्डितोत्तमः।
मेने सर्वपुरुषार्थसारं श्रीनाममङ्गलम्॥१०॥

*tacchrutvā harṣito vipraḥ śrīvāsaḥ paṇḍitottamaḥ|*
*mene sarvapuruṣārthasāraṁ śrīnāmamaṅgalam||10||*

*Word for word:* tat — that; shrutva — hearing; harshitah — delighted; viprah — the brahmana; shrivasah — Srivasa; pandita-uttamah — the best of pandits; mene — considered; sarva-purusha-artha-saram — the essence of all human goals; shri-nama-mangalam — the auspicious holy name.

**10.** Hearing this, the brahmana Srivasa, the best of pandits, rejoiced and recognized the auspicious holy name as the essence of all the aims of human life.

### Verse 11

हरिसङ्कीर्तनं कृत्वा नगरे नगरे प्रभुः।
म्लेच्छादीनुद्दधारासौ जगतामीश्वरो हरिः॥११॥

*harisaṅkīrtanaṁ kṛtvā nagare nagare prabhuḥ|*
*mlecchādīnuddadhārāsau jagatāmīśvaro hariḥ||11||*

*Word for word:* hari-sankirtanam — the sankirtana of Hari; kritva — performing; nagare nagare — in town after town; prabhuh — the Lord; mlechchha-adin — the mlechchhas and others; uddadhara — delivered; asau — He; jagatam — of the worlds; ishvarah — the Sovereign; harih — Hari.

**11.** Thus, performing the sankirtana of Hari in town after town, the Lord — Hari, the Sovereign of the worlds — delivered the mlechchhas and others.

### Verse 12

एकदा भगवानाह नेत्रवारिभराप्लुतः।
स्थातुं नाहं समर्थोऽस्मि गच्छामि मथुरां पुरीम्॥१२॥

*ekadā bhagavānāha netravāribharāplutaḥ|*
*sthātuṁ nāhaṁ samartho'smi gacchāmi mathurāṁ purīm||12||*

*Word for word:* ekada — once; bhagavan — Bhagavan; aha — said; netra-vari-bhara-aplutah — flooded with a stream of tears; sthatum — to stay; na — not; aham — I; samarthah asmi — am able; gachchhami — I am going; mathuram — to Mathura; purim — the city.

**12.** One day Bhagavan, bathed in tears, said, "I can no longer stay here. I am going to the city of Mathura."

### Verse 13

छित्त्वा यज्ञोपवीतं स्वं कृष्णविश्लेषकातरः।
श्रुत्वा तद्वचनं तस्य प्राह वैद्यो मुरारिकः॥१३॥

*chittvā yajñopavītaṁ svaṁ kṛṣṇaviśleṣakātaraḥ|*
*śrutvā tadvacanaṁ tasya prāha vaidyo murārikaḥ||13||*

*Word for word:* chhittva — breaking; yajna-upavitam — the sacred thread; svam — His own; krishna-vishlesha-katarah — distraught at separation from Krishna; shrutva — hearing; tat — those; vachanam — words; tasya — His; praha — said; vaidyah — the physician; murarikah — (humble) Murari.

**13.** In the anguish of separation from Krishna He broke His sacred thread[^217-4]. Hearing His words, the humble physician Murari said:

### Verse 14

भगवन्सकलं कर्तुं शक्तोऽसि सर्वतत्त्ववित्।
गन्तुं स्थातुं त्वमार्येण तथापि नार्हसि ध्रुवम्॥१४॥

*bhagavansakalaṁ kartuṁ śakto'si sarvatattvavit|*
*gantuṁ sthātuṁ tvamāryeṇa tathāpi nārhasi dhruvam||14||*

*Word for word:* bhagavan — O Bhagavan; sakalam — everything; kartum — to do; shaktah asi — You are able; sarva-tattva-vit — knower of all truths; gantum — to go; sthatum — to stay; tvam — You; aryena — by (the way of) the noble; tatha api — even so; na arhasi — You ought not; dhruvam — surely.

**14.** "Bhagavan, You can do anything, You know all truths; You are free to go or to stay. Even so, by the way of the noble[^217-5], You surely ought not to go.

### Verse 15

त्वया चेत्क्रियते नाथ स्वातन्त्र्यात्सकला जनाः।
स्वातन्त्र्येण करिष्यन्ति पतिष्यन्त्यशुचौ पुनः॥१५॥

*tvayā cetkriyate nātha svātantryātsakalā janāḥ|*
*svātantryeṇa kariṣyanti patiṣyantyaśucau punaḥ||15||*

*Word for word:* tvaya — by You; chet — if; kriyate — it is done; natha — O Lord; svatantryat — out of independence; sakalah — all; janah — people; svatantryena — independently; karishyanti — will act; patishyanti — will fall; ashuchau — into impurity; punah — then.

**15.** If You, O Lord, act as You alone will, then all people too will act as they will — and fall into impurity.

### Verse 16

एतन्मत्वा स्वयं तात स्वाश्रमादाश्रमान्तरम्।
कर्तव्यं तु त्वया ते के कथयन्तु महत्तमाः॥१६॥

*etanmatvā svayaṁ tāta svāśramādāśramāntaram|*
*kartavyaṁ tu tvayā te ke kathayantu mahattamāḥ||16||*

*Word for word:* etat — this; matva — considering; svayam — Yourself; tata — dear one; sva-ashramat — from Your own ashrama; ashrama-antaram — (a change) to another ashrama; kartavyam — is to be made; tu — but; tvaya — by You; te ke — who are they; kathayantu — let them say; mahattamah — the greatest.

**16.** Consider this, dear one: that You Yourself should pass from Your own ashrama into another — which of the greatest would say it must be so?

### Verse 17

कृत्वैव गमनं तेऽद्य कृतं स्यात्सर्वदेहिनाम्।
चैतन्यरहितानां च किं तावत्कथयामि ते॥१७॥

*kṛtvaiva gamanaṁ te'dya kṛtaṁ syātsarvadehinām|*
*caitanyarahitānāṁ ca kiṁ tāvatkathayāmi te||17||*

*Word for word:* kritva eva — once making; gamanam — departure; te — Your; adya — today; kritam syat — it would be all over; sarva-dehinam — for all embodied beings; chaitanya-rahitanam — bereft of consciousness (of Chaitanya); cha — and; kim — what; tavat — more; kathayami — shall I say; te — to You.

**17.** Should You leave today, it will be the end of all embodied beings: they will be left without Chaitanya, without consciousness[^217-6]. What more can I say to You?"

### Verse 18

भक्तैः संवेष्टितो नित्यं नित्यानन्दसमन्वितः।
गदाधरेण गन्धाद्यैः सेवितो भक्तगो हरिः॥१८॥

*bhaktaiḥ saṁveṣṭito nityaṁ nityānandasamanvitaḥ|*
*gadādhareṇa gandhādyaiḥ sevito bhaktago hariḥ||18||*

*Word for word:* bhaktaih — by devotees; samveshtitah — surrounded; nityam — always; nityananda-samanvitah — accompanied by Nityananda; gadadharena — by Gadadhara; gandha-adyaih — with fragrances and so on; sevitah — served; bhakta-gah — abiding among His devotees; harih — Hari.

**18.** Hari was ever surrounded by His devotees, Nityananda was with Him, and Gadadhara served Him with fragrances and other offerings — for He dwells among His devotees[^217-7].

### Verse 19

तच्छ्रुत्वा भगवांस्तूष्णीं भूत्वासीत्प्रेमविह्वलः।
कृष्णसङ्कीर्तनानन्दपूर्णमनोरथः स्वयम्॥१९॥

*tacchrutvā bhagavāṁstūṣṇīṁ bhūtvāsītpremavihvalaḥ|*
*kṛṣṇasaṅkīrtanānandapūrṇamanorathaḥ svayam||19||*

*Word for word:* tat — that; shrutva — hearing; bhagavan — Bhagavan; tushnim bhutva — falling silent; asit — remained; prema-vihvalah — overwhelmed by love; krishna-sankirtana-ananda-purna-manorathah — His desires fulfilled by the bliss of Krishna's sankirtana; svayam — Himself.

**19.** Hearing Murari's words, Bhagavan fell silent, overwhelmed by love; all His desires were fulfilled in the bliss of Krishna's sankirtana.

*Thus ends the seventeenth sarga, "The Admonition of Sri Murari Gupta," of the second prakrama of the poem "Sri Krishna Chaitanya Charitamrita."*

[^217-1]: Chandrashekhara Acharyaratna was the Lord's maternal uncle; the play described in sargas 2.15–16 was staged in his house.
[^217-2]: Srivasa asks: if the chanting of the name is declared specifically for the Kali age, are the ways of the other ages not inferior to it? The Lord's answer (vv. 7–9) shows that in every age the same fruit is attained, but in Kali the Lord comes Himself — as the holy name.
[^217-3]: The name of Hari is not different from Hari Himself.
[^217-4]: The sacred thread is the mark of the twice-born householder; by breaking it the Lord foreshadows His leaving home and accepting sannyasa.
[^217-5]: The reading and sense of this passage are not entirely clear.
[^217-6]: A play on words: "bereft of consciousness" in Sanskrit is "bereft of chaitanya."
[^217-7]: Literally "going with the devotees" (bhakta-ga).

## Prakrama 2, Sarga 18. The Prelude to Sannyasa

*In a dream the Lord is given the mantra of sannyasa; Keshava Bharati comes to Navadvipa; the Lord consoles Srivasa, instructs Murari, and in Kantakanagara accepts sannyasa. End of the second prakrama*

### Verse 1

ततः कियद्दिने प्राह भगवान्कार्यमानुषः।
स्वप्ने दृष्टो मया कश्चिदागत्य ब्राह्मणोत्तमः॥१॥

*tataḥ kiyaddine prāha bhagavānkāryamānuṣaḥ|*
*svapne dṛṣṭo mayā kaścidāgatya brāhmaṇottamaḥ||1||*

*Word for word:* tatah — then; kiyat-dine — after some days; praha — said; bhagavan — Bhagavan; karya-manushah — human for the sake of (His) task; svapne — in a dream; drishtah — was seen; maya — by Me; kashchit — a certain; agatya — coming; brahmana-uttamah — excellent brahmana.

**1.** Some days later Bhagavan, who had taken a human form for the sake of His mission, said, "I dreamt that a certain excellent brahmana came to Me,

### Verse 2

सन्न्यासमन्त्रं मत्कर्णे कथयामास सुस्मितः।
तच्छ्रुत्वा व्यथितो रात्रौ दिवा चाहं विरोदिमि॥२॥

*sannyāsamantraṁ matkarṇe kathayāmāsa susmitaḥ|*
*tacchrutvā vyathito rātrau divā cāhaṁ virodimi||2||*

*Word for word:* sannyasa-mantram — the mantra of sannyasa; mat-karne — into My ear; kathayam asa — spoke; su-smitah — smiling sweetly; tat — that; shrutva — hearing; vyathitah — pained; ratrau — by night; diva — by day; cha — and; aham — I; virodimi — weep.

**2.** and, smiling sweetly, spoke the mantra of sannyasa into My ear. Since hearing it I have been grieving, weeping by night and by day.

### Verse 3

कथं प्रियं हरिं नाथं त्यक्त्वान्यदुचितं मम।
मुरारिः प्राह तच्छ्रुत्वा तन्मन्त्रे भगवान्स्वयम्॥३॥

*kathaṁ priyaṁ hariṁ nāthaṁ tyaktvānyaducitaṁ mama|*
*murāriḥ prāha tacchrutvā tanmantre bhagavānsvayam||3||*

*Word for word:* katham — how; priyam — the dear; harim — Hari; natham — the Lord; tyaktva — abandoning; anyat — something else; uchitam — is fitting; mama — for Me; murarih — Murari; praha — said; tat — that; shrutva — hearing; tat-mantre — in that mantra; bhagavan — Bhagavan; svayam — Himself.

**3.** How can I abandon dear Hari, My Lord? What else could befit Me?" Hearing this, Murari said, "In that mantra is Bhagavan Himself.

### Verse 4

षष्ठीसमासं मनसा विचिन्त्य त्वं सुखी भव॥४॥

*ṣaṣṭhīsamāsaṁ manasā vicintya tvaṁ sukhī bhava||4||*

*Word for word:* shashthi-samasam — a compound in the sixth (genitive) case; manasa — in the mind; vichintya — considering; tvam — You; sukhi — happy; bhava — be.

**4.** Understand it in Your mind as a compound in the genitive case, and be happy[^218-1]."

### Verse 5

तत्रोवाच प्रभुर्वाचं तथापि खिद्यते मनः।
शब्दशक्त्या करिष्यामि किमित्युक्त्वा रुरोद सः॥५॥

*tatrovāca prabhurvācaṁ tathāpi khidyate manaḥ|*
*śabdaśaktyā kariṣyāmi kimityuktvā ruroda saḥ||5||*

*Word for word:* tatra — to that; uvacha — spoke; prabhuh — the Lord; vacham — a word; tatha api — still; khidyate — is distressed; manah — the mind; shabda-shaktya — by the power of words; karishyami — shall I do; kim — what; iti — thus; uktva — saying; ruroda — wept; sah — He.

**5.** To this the Lord replied, "Still My mind is troubled. What am I to do with the power of words?[^218-2]" And saying this, He wept.

### Verse 6

तच्छ्रुत्वा व्यथिताः सर्वे कृष्णविश्लेषकातराः।
यथा भाविनि माथुरे विक्लवा व्रजसुभ्रुवः॥६॥

*tacchrutvā vyathitāḥ sarve kṛṣṇaviśleṣakātarāḥ|*
*yathā bhāvini māthure viklavā vrajasubhruvaḥ||6||*

*Word for word:* tat — that; shrutva — hearing; vyathitah — were pained; sarve — all; krishna-vishlesha-katarah — distraught at (the coming) separation from Krishna; yatha — as; bhavini — when impending; mathure — (the journey) to Mathura; viklavah — distraught; vraja-subhruvah — the fair-browed maidens of Vraja.

**6.** Hearing this, all were stricken, distraught at the coming separation from Krishna — like the fair-browed maidens of Vraja, distraught when Krishna's journey to Mathura was at hand.

*Word for word:* iti — thus; hareh — of Hari; charitam — the deeds; samshrinoti — hears; yah — who; sapadi — at once; papa-ganam — the host of sins; parihaya — casting off; sah — he; vishati — enters; pada-tale — at the soles of the feet; nrihareh — of Nrihari; labhet — will gain; atula-bhaktim — incomparable devotion; asangam — detachment; anaryatah — from the ignoble.

**33.** Whoever thus hears the deeds of Hari at once casts off the host of his sins and comes to the soles of Nrihari's feet; he will gain incomparable devotion and freedom from attachment to all that is ignoble.

*Thus ends the eighteenth sarga, "The Prelude to Sannyasa" (Sannyasa-sutra), of the second prakrama of the poem "Sri Krishna Chaitanya Charitamrita." Thus the second prakrama is complete.*

[^218-1]: Murari suggests interpreting the sannyasa mantra, which speaks of identity with Brahman, through the genitive case: not "I am He" but "I am His," that is, the Lord's servant. This is how the Gaudiya Vaishnava tradition understands the great sayings of the Upanishads.
[^218-2]: That is, the interpretation does not remove the direct sense of the mantra's words.
[^218-3]: The word sadhu here, as commonly in Bengal, means a merchant engaged in overseas trade.
[^218-4]: The sense is unfolded in v. 29: the Lord bids Murari to serve Advaita Acharya diligently. It may also be understood as "you are always detached — so carry out My word."
[^218-5]: Kantaka (Kantakanagara) is present-day Katwa on the bank of the Ganga.

## Prakrama 3, Sarga 1. The Words of the Women of Kantakanagara

*Damodara asks Murari to tell of the Lord's sannyasa; verses of invocation; the Lord leaves Navadvipa; Chandrashekhara returns and tells how the people of Kantakanagara gazed at the Lord and what the women said of Him*

**16.** This handsome youth has conquered Kamadeva with his beauty and surpassed the very lord of speech[^301-8] with his words. Some woman, by her good deeds, became his wife — and by some deeds, it seems, she now pines in separation!

### Verse 17

मातास्य पुत्रस्य मुखं न दृष्ट्वा
जीवत्यजीवा बहुदुःखतप्ता।
यथा हि कृष्णो मथुरां दिदृक्षु-
र्गतो व्रजस्थाश्च बभूवुरार्ताः॥१७॥

*mātāsya putrasya mukhaṁ na dṛṣṭvā*
*jīvatyajīvā bahuduḥkhataptā|*
*yathā hi kṛṣṇo mathurāṁ didṛkṣu-*
*rgato vrajasthāśca babhūvurārtāḥ||17||*

*Word for word:* mata — the mother; asya — of this; putrasya — son; mukham — the face; na drishtva — not seeing; jivati — lives; ajiva — lifeless; bahu-duhkha-tapta — burning with many sorrows; yatha — as; hi — indeed; krishnah — Krishna; mathuram — Mathura; didrikshuh — wishing to see; gatah — went; vraja-sthah — the people of Vraja; cha — and; babhuvuh — became; artah — stricken.

**17.** His mother, not seeing her son's face, lives on as one lifeless, burning with many sorrows — as the people of Vraja grieved when Krishna went away, wishing to see Mathura.'

### Verse 18

काश्चिद्विदग्धाः स्फुटमेव चाहु-
र्गोपाङ्गनाभावविभावितोऽसौ।
श्रीनन्दपुत्रः स्वयमाविरासी-
त्सन्न्यासवेशेन स्वकार्यसाधकः॥१८॥

*kāścidvidagdhāḥ sphuṭameva cāhu-*
*rgopāṅganābhāvavibhāvito'sau|*
*śrīnandaputraḥ svayamāvirāsī-*
*tsannyāsaveśena svakāryasādhakaḥ||18||*

*Word for word:* kashchit — some; vidagdhah — discerning; sphutam eva — plainly; cha — and; ahuh — said; gopa-angana-bhava-vibhavitah — imbued with the feelings of the cowherd women; asau — this; shri-nanda-putrah — the son of Sri Nanda; svayam — Himself; avirasit — has appeared; sannyasa-veshena — in the dress of a sannyasi; sva-karya-sadhakah — accomplishing His own purpose.

**18.** And others, more discerning, said plainly, 'This is the son of Sri Nanda Himself, imbued with the feelings of the cowherd women, who has appeared in the dress of a sannyasi to accomplish His own purpose.'

### Verse 19

एवंविधान्या बहुधा सुवाचो
बभूवुरन्योन्यकथाप्रसङ्गैः।
मुखं पिबन्त्यो न विदुः स्वदेहं
विश्वम्भरस्याम्बुजलोचनस्य॥१९॥

*evaṁvidhānyā bahudhā suvāco*
*babhūvuranyonyakathāprasaṅgaiḥ|*
*mukhaṁ pibantyo na viduḥ svadehaṁ*
*viśvambharasyāmbujalocanasya||19||*

*Word for word:* evam-vidhah — such; anyah — other; bahudha — many; su-vachah — fair words; babhuvuh — arose; anyonya-katha-prasangaih — in their talk with one another; mukham — the face; pibantyah — drinking in; na viduh — were unaware; sva-deham — of their own bodies; vishvambharasya — of Vishvambhara; ambuja-lochanasya — the lotus-eyed.

**19.** Many such fair words and others besides passed in their talk with one another; drinking in the face of lotus-eyed Vishvambhara, they forgot their own bodies."

*Thus ends the first sarga, "The Words of the Women of Kantakanagara" (Kantakanagara-nagari-vachana), of the third prakrama of the poem "Sri Krishna Chaitanya Charitamrita."*

[^301-1]: Damodara Pandita, who questions Murari: the poem is framed as their dialogue.
[^301-2]: Purushottama is Puri, the city of Jagannatha.
[^301-3]: The syntax of the second half of the verse is not entirely clear; the translation gives the probable sense.
[^301-4]: Shankara is Shiva.
[^301-5]: The Ganga.
[^301-6]: The reading is conjectural.
[^301-7]: Mukunda is here a name of the Lord Himself.
[^301-8]: The lord of speech is Brihaspati, the preceptor of the gods.

## Prakrama 3, Sarga 2. The Purification of the Ashrama of Sannyasa

*The Lord asks the people of Kantakanagara for their blessing; in the dwelling of Keshava Bharati He "initiates" His guru into the mantra of sannyasa and accepts sannyasa; guru and disciple dance in kirtana*

### Verse 1

नृत्यावसाने भगवान्रुरोद
प्रेम्णा हरेः सोऽपि विभिन्नधैर्यः।
दृष्ट्वा तदा तत्र समागता वै
रुदन्ति ते प्रेमजलाविलाक्षाः॥१॥

*nṛtyāvasāne bhagavānruroda*
*premṇā hareḥ so'pi vibhinnadhairyaḥ|*
*dṛṣṭvā tadā tatra samāgatā vai*
*rudanti te premajalāvilākṣāḥ||1||*

*Word for word:* nritya-avasane — at the end of the dance; bhagavan — Bhagavan; ruroda — wept; premna — out of love; hareh — for Hari; sah — He; api — too; vibhinna-dhairyah — His composure shattered; drishtva — seeing; tada — then; tatra — there; samagatah — those assembled; vai — indeed; rudanti — weep; te — they; prema-jala-avila-akshah — their eyes clouded with tears of love.

**1.** When the dance was over, Bhagavan wept: love for Hari had shattered His composure. Seeing this, all who had gathered there wept too, their eyes clouded with tears of love.

### Verse 2

ततः समुत्थाय हरिः सगद्गद-
स्वरेण तान्प्राह समागताञ्जनान्।
मां तात मातश्च विधेहि साम्प्रतं
शुभाशिषो येन हरिस्मृतिः स्यात्॥२॥

*tataḥ samutthāya hariḥ sagadgada-*
*svareṇa tānprāha samāgatāñjanān|*
*māṁ tāta mātaśca vidhehi sāmprataṁ*
*śubhāśiṣo yena harismṛtiḥ syāt||2||*

*Word for word:* tatah — then; samutthaya — rising; harih — Hari; sa-gadgada-svarena — in a faltering voice; tan — to those; praha — said; samagatan — assembled; janan — people; mam — on Me; tata — fathers; matah — mothers; cha — and; vidhehi — bestow; sampratam — now; shubha-ashishah — auspicious blessings; yena — so that; hari-smritih — remembrance of Hari; syat — may be.

**2.** Then Hari rose and in a faltering voice said to the assembled people, "Fathers and mothers, bless Me now, so that I may always remember Hari."

### Verse 3

श्रुत्वाभिलज्जाकुलिता विवस्त्रा
गतास्ततस्ते प्ररुदन्त एव।
श्रीकृष्णप्रेमापरिपूर्णदेहा
बभूवुः सद्भक्तिरसेन पूर्णाः॥३॥

*śrutvābhilajjākulitā vivastrā*
*gatāstataste prarudanta eva|*
*śrīkṛṣṇapremāparipūrṇadehā*
*babhūvuḥ sadbhaktirasena pūrṇāḥ||3||*

*Word for word:* shrutva — hearing; abhilajja-akulitah — overcome with shame; vivastrah — as if stripped bare; gatah — went; tatah — from there; te — they; prarudantah — weeping; eva — all the while; shri-krishna-prema-aparipurna-dehah — their bodies wholly filled with love for Sri Krishna; babhuvuh — became; sat-bhakti-rasena — with the rasa of true devotion; purnah — filled.

**3.** Hearing this, they were overcome with shame, as if stripped bare[^302-1], and went away from there, weeping all the while; their bodies were filled with love for Sri Krishna, and they themselves with the rasa of true devotion.

### Verse 4

तान्सान्त्वयित्वा निजदर्शनामृतैः
स गौरचन्द्रो भगवाञ्जगाम।
गुरोर्निवासं सह वैष्णवाग्र्यैः
श्रीकेशवाख्यस्य महानुभावः॥४॥

*tānsāntvayitvā nijadarśanāmṛtaiḥ*
*sa gauracandro bhagavāñjagāma|*
*gurornivāsaṁ saha vaiṣṇavāgryaiḥ*
*śrīkeśavākhyasya mahānubhāvaḥ||4||*

*Word for word:* tan — them; santvayitva — consoling; nija-darshana-amritaih — with the nectar of the sight of Himself; sah — He; gaurachandrah — Gaurachandra; bhagavan — Bhagavan; jagama — went; guroh — of the guru; nivasam — to the dwelling; saha — together; vaishnava-agryaih — with the foremost Vaishnavas; shri-keshava-akhyasya — named Sri Keshava; maha-anubhavah — the great-souled.

**4.** Having consoled them with the nectar of the sight of Himself, the great-souled Bhagavan Gaurachandra went with the foremost Vaishnavas to the dwelling of the guru named Sri Keshava.

### Verse 5

नत्वा गुरोः पादयुगं निवासं
तस्मिन्स चक्रे करुणाम्बुधिर्हरिः।
श्रीरामनारायणनाममङ्गलं
गायन्गुणान्प्रेमविभिन्नधैर्यः॥५॥

*natvā guroḥ pādayugaṁ nivāsaṁ*
*tasminsa cakre karuṇāmbudhirhariḥ|*
*śrīrāmanārāyaṇanāmamaṅgalaṁ*
*gāyanguṇānpremavibhinnadhairyaḥ||5||*

*Word for word:* natva — bowing; guroh — of the guru; pada-yugam — to the pair of feet; nivasam chakre — took up His stay; tasmin — there; sah — He; karuna-ambudhih — the ocean of mercy; harih — Hari; shri-rama-narayana-nama-mangalam — the auspicious names of Sri Rama and Narayana; gayan — singing; gunan — the qualities; prema-vibhinna-dhairyah — His composure shattered by love.

**5.** Bowing to His guru's feet, Hari, the ocean of mercy, stayed there; He sang the auspicious names of Sri Rama and Narayana and Their qualities, and love shattered His composure.

### Verse 6

तथापराह्णे नृहरेरवाप्त्यै
न्यासोक्तकर्माणि चकार शुद्धः।
आचार्यरत्नो भगवांश्चकार
कृष्णस्य पूजां विधिवद्विधिज्ञः॥६॥

*tathāparāhṇe nṛhareravāptyai*
*nyāsoktakarmāṇi cakāra śuddhaḥ|*
*ācāryaratno bhagavāṁścakāra*
*kṛṣṇasya pūjāṁ vidhivadvidhijñaḥ||6||*

*Word for word:* tatha — then; aparahne — in the afternoon; nrihareh — of Nrihari; avaptyai — for the attainment; nyasa-ukta-karmani — the rites prescribed for sannyasa; chakara — performed; shuddhah — pure; acharyaratnah — the Acharyaratna; bhagavan — the venerable; chakara — performed; krishnasya — to Krishna; pujam — worship; vidhi-vat — according to rule; vidhi-jnah — versed in the rules.

**6.** In the afternoon He, the pure one, performed the rites prescribed for sannyasa, so as to attain Nrihari[^302-2], while the venerable Acharyaratna, versed in the injunctions, duly performed the worship of Krishna.

### Verse 7

ततः समीपं स गुरोर्हितार्थी
गत्वावदत्कर्णसमीप ईशः।
स्वप्ने मया मन्त्रवरो हि लब्धः
शृणुष्व तत्किं तव सम्मतं स्यात्॥७॥

*tataḥ samīpaṁ sa gurorhitārthī*
*gatvāvadatkarṇasamīpa īśaḥ|*
*svapne mayā mantravaro hi labdhaḥ*
*śṛṇuṣva tatkiṁ tava sammataṁ syāt||7||*

*Word for word:* tatah — then; samipam — near; sah — He; guroh — to the guru; hita-arthi — seeking (his) good; gatva — going; avadat — said; karna-samipe — into his ear; ishah — the Lord; svapne — in a dream; maya — by Me; mantra-varah — an excellent mantra; hi — indeed; labdhah — was received; shrinushva — hear; tat — it; kim — whether; tava — by you; sammatam — approved; syat — it may be.

**7.** Then the Lord, seeking His guru's good, went up to him and said into his ear, "In a dream I received an excellent mantra. Hear it — will you approve of it?"

### Verse 8

वारत्रयं तच्छ्रवणान्तिकं स्वयं
प्रोवाच न्यासोक्तमनुं विशुद्धम्।
श्रुत्वावदत्सोऽपि हरेरिदं स्या-
त्सन्न्यासमन्त्रं परमं पवित्रम्॥८॥

*vāratrayaṁ tacchravaṇāntikaṁ svayaṁ*
*provāca nyāsoktamanuṁ viśuddham|*
*śrutvāvadatso'pi hareridaṁ syā-*
*tsannyāsamantraṁ paramaṁ pavitram||8||*

*Word for word:* vara-trayam — three times; tat-shravana-antikam — close to his ear; svayam — Himself; provacha — spoke; nyasa-ukta-manum — the mantra prescribed for sannyasa; vishuddham — pure; shrutva — hearing; avadat — said; sah — he; api — too; hareh — to Hari; idam — this; syat — must be; sannyasa-mantram — the mantra of sannyasa; paramam — supreme; pavitram — purifying.

**8.** And three times He Himself spoke into his very ear the pure mantra prescribed for sannyasa. Hearing it, the other replied to Hari, "This is indeed the mantra of sannyasa, supreme and purifying."

### Verse 9

व्याजेन दीक्षां गुरवे स दत्त्वा
लोकैकनाथो गुरुरव्ययात्मा।
गुरो ददस्वाद्य मनीषितं मे
सन्न्यासमित्याह पुटाञ्जलिः प्रभुः॥९॥

*vyājena dīkṣāṁ gurave sa dattvā*
*lokaikanātho gururavyayātmā|*
*guro dadasvādya manīṣitaṁ me*
*sannyāsamityāha puṭāñjaliḥ prabhuḥ||9||*

*Word for word:* vyajena — under a pretext; diksham — initiation; gurave — to the guru; sah — He; dattva — having given; loka-eka-nathah — the one Lord of the worlds; guruh — the guru; avyaya-atma — the changeless Self; guro — O guru; dadasva — give; adya — today; manishitam — longed-for; me — to Me; sannyasam — sannyasa; iti — thus; aha — said; puta-anjalih — with joined palms; prabhuh — the Lord.

**9.** Thus the one Lord of the worlds, the changeless, eternal guru, under a pretext gave initiation to His own guru[^302-3]. And with joined palms the Lord said, "O guru, grant Me today the sannyasa I long for."

### Verse 10

ततः शुभे सङ्क्रमणे रवेः क्षणे
कुम्भं प्रयाति मकरान्मनीषी।
सन्न्यासमन्त्रं प्रददौ महात्मा
श्रीकेशवाख्यो हरये विधानवित्॥१०॥

*tataḥ śubhe saṅkramaṇe raveḥ kṣaṇe*
*kumbhaṁ prayāti makarānmanīṣī|*
*sannyāsamantraṁ pradadau mahātmā*
*śrīkeśavākhyo haraye vidhānavit||10||*

*Word for word:* tatah — then; shubhe — at the auspicious; sankramane — transit; raveh — of the sun; kshane — at the moment; kumbham — into Aquarius; prayati — as it passes; makarat — from Capricorn; manishi — the wise; sannyasa-mantram — the mantra of sannyasa; pradadau — gave; maha-atma — the great soul; shri-keshava-akhyah — named Sri Keshava; haraye — to Hari; vidhana-vit — versed in the rite.

**10.** And at the auspicious moment when the sun passes from Capricorn into Aquarius[^302-4], the wise Sri Keshava, a great soul versed in the rite, gave Hari the mantra of sannyasa.

### Verse 11

ततः सरोमाञ्चितदेहयष्टि-
रानन्दनेत्राम्बुभिरार्द्रवक्षाः।
संन्यस्त एवाहमिति स्वयं हरिः
सगद्गदं वाक्यमुवाच देवः॥११॥

*tataḥ saromāñcitadehayaṣṭi-*
*rānandanetrāmbubhirārdravakṣāḥ|*
*saṁnyasta evāhamiti svayaṁ hariḥ*
*sagadgadaṁ vākyamuvāca devaḥ||11||*

*Word for word:* tatah — then; sa-romanchita-deha-yashtih — His slender body thrilling with rapture; ananda-netra-ambubhih — with tears of bliss from His eyes; ardra-vakshah — His chest wet; samnyastah — renounced; eva — truly; aham — I; iti — thus; svayam — Himself; harih — Hari; sa-gadgadam — in a faltering voice; vakyam — the words; uvacha — spoke; devah — the Lord.

**11.** And then Hari's slender body thrilled with rapture, His chest grew wet with tears of bliss, and the Lord Himself said in a faltering voice, "I have truly renounced the world!"

### Verse 12

गच्छन्तमालोक्य हरिं गुरुः स्वयं
दण्डं सचेलं त्वरया ददौ करे।
भो भो गृहाणेति वदन्गुरोर्वचः
श्रुत्वा गृहीत्वा गुरुभक्तिलम्पटः॥१२॥

*gacchantamālokya hariṁ guruḥ svayaṁ*
*daṇḍaṁ sacelaṁ tvarayā dadau kare|*
*bho bho gṛhāṇeti vadangurorvacaḥ*
*śrutvā gṛhītvā gurubhaktilampaṭaḥ||12||*

*Word for word:* gachchhantam — going away; alokya — seeing; harim — Hari; guruh — the guru; svayam — himself; dandam — the staff; sa-chelam — with the cloth; tvaraya — hastily; dadau — placed; kare — in His hand; bho bho — ho there; grihana — take; iti — thus; vadan — saying; guroh — of the guru; vachah — the word; shrutva — hearing; grihitva — taking (it); guru-bhakti-lampatah — eager in devotion to the guru.

**12.** Seeing Hari about to leave, the guru himself hastily placed the staff, together with the cloth, in His hand, saying, "Ho there, ho there, take it!" Hearing the guru's word, Hari, eager in devotion to His guru, accepted them,

### Verse 13

गुरोर्निदेशं बहुमन्यमान-
स्तत्रावसत्तद्दिवसं जितारिः।
रात्रौ वसन्कीर्तनमाशु चक्रे
नृत्यं च तस्मिन्गुरुणा समं प्रभुः॥१३॥

*gurornideśaṁ bahumanyamāna-*
*statrāvasattaddivasaṁ jitāriḥ|*
*rātrau vasankīrtanamāśu cakre*
*nṛtyaṁ ca tasminguruṇā samaṁ prabhuḥ||13||*

*Word for word:* guroh — of the guru; nidesham — the command; bahu-manyamanah — honouring highly; tatra — there; avasat — stayed; tat-divasam — that day; jita-arih — the conqueror of foes; ratrau — at night; vasan — staying; kirtanam — kirtana; ashu — soon; chakre — began; nrityam — dancing; cha — and; tasmin — there; guruna samam — together with the guru; prabhuh — the Lord.

**13.** and, honouring His guru's command, He, the conqueror of foes, stayed there that day. And at night the Lord soon began kirtana and dancing there together with the guru.

### Verse 14

ननर्त तस्मिञ्जगतां गुरोर्गुरुः
कृष्णेन सार्धं महता सुखेन।
आनन्दपूर्णस्तु पुनः स मेने
ब्राह्मं सुखं तुच्छतरं महात्मा॥१४॥

*nanarta tasmiñjagatāṁ gurorguruḥ*
*kṛṣṇena sārdhaṁ mahatā sukhena|*
*ānandapūrṇastu punaḥ sa mene*
*brāhmaṁ sukhaṁ tucchataraṁ mahātmā||14||*

*Word for word:* nanarta — danced; tasmin — there; jagatam — of the worlds; guroh — of the guru; guruh — the guru; krishnena sardham — together with Krishna; mahata — with great; sukhena — happiness; ananda-purnah — filled with bliss; tu — and; punah — then; sah — he; mene — considered; brahmam — of Brahman; sukham — the happiness; tuchchha-taram — most paltry; maha-atma — the great soul.

**14.** There the guru of the Guru of the worlds[^302-5] danced together with Krishna in great happiness; filled with bliss, the great soul now held the happiness of Brahman to be utterly paltry.

### Verse 15

नृत्यावसाने हरिमब्रवीत्स
कोऽपीह मे दण्डमिमं कराग्रात्।
आकृष्य मां प्राह भुजद्वयेन
स्पृष्ट्वा स्वयं त्वं नटनं कुरुष्व॥१५॥

*nṛtyāvasāne harimabravītsa*
*ko'pīha me daṇḍamimaṁ karāgrāt|*

[^302-1]: Literally "naked"; probably an image of shame: the Lord asks a blessing of them, His servants. The reading may be corrupt.
[^302-2]: Nrihari is here Krishna: Gaura, playing the part of a devotee, accepts sannyasa in order to attain Him.
[^302-3]: The Lord Himself speaks the mantra into Keshava Bharati's ear, as though initiating him, and only then receives it from him.
[^302-4]: That is, at the end of the solar month of Magha (January–February).
[^302-5]: Keshava Bharati, who became the guru of Krishna Chaitanya, the Guru of all the worlds.
[^302-6]: Hence the title of the sarga: sannyasa, accepted by the Lord and filled with love, purifies the very order of sannyasa.

## Prakrama 3, Sarga 3. Wandering in the Radha Country

*atha natvā guroḥ pādaṁ tamanujñāpya mādhavaḥ|*

**1.** Then Madhava bowed to His guru's feet, took leave of him and, at his command, set out, keeping Himself hidden, for the Radha country. The mighty-armed one

**20.** Sri Krishna will come to the Acharya's house[^303-5], perhaps the day after tomorrow; there you will surely see Him.

हरेर्गुणं सर्वसुखप्रदं नृणाम्॥२१॥

*iti śrutaṁ śrīharikīrtanādikaṁ*

*Word for word:* iti — thus; shrutam — heard; shri-hari-kirtana-adikam — the chanting of Sri Hari and the rest; maya — by me; cha — and; drishtam — seen; bhagavat-kritam — done by Bhagavan; shubham — auspicious; samagram — in full; etat — this; kathitam — has been told; su-mangalam — most auspicious; hareh — of Hari; gunam — the glory; sarva-sukha-pradam — granting every happiness; nrinam — to men.

**21.** Thus have I heard and seen the auspicious chanting of Sri Hari and the other deeds of Bhagavan, and I have told it all in full. This blessed account of Hari's glory grants every happiness to men.

*Thus ends the third sarga, "Wandering in the Radha Country" (Radhadesha-bhramana), of the third prakrama of the poem "Sri Krishna Chaitanya Charitamrita."*

[^303-1]: From here to the end of the sarga the narrator is Chandrashekhara Acharyaratna, who has returned to the devotees in Navadvipa (cf. Sargas 3.1 and 3.4).
[^303-2]: The Abode of Shri (Shriniketana) — an epithet of the Lord as the abode of the goddess Lakshmi.
[^303-3]: "Obeisance to Narayana" — the customary greeting of sannyasis: having become a sannyasi, the Lord sends the devotees a greeting according to the rule of His new ashrama.
[^303-4]: Apparently the Lord Himself, who has just accepted sannyasa (cf. v. 12).
[^303-5]: Advaita Acharya's, at Shantipura.

## Prakrama 3, Sarga 4. Pastimes at Sri Advaita's House

*The devotees of Navadvipa lament the Lord's sannyasa; Nityananda brings Shachi and the Vaishnavas to Advaita's house; the Lord comes there and spends a day and a night with them in kirtana, takes leave of Haridasa, Advaita and Gopinatha Acharya, and departs for Purushottama*

### Verse 1

आचार्यरत्नाद्धि निशम्य तद्वचो
हरेर्गुणास्वादविभिन्नधैर्याः।
आर्तस्वरैर्वा रुरुदुः सुदुःखिता
अद्वैतमुख्या द्विजसज्जनास्ततः॥१॥

*ācāryaratnāddhi niśamya tadvaco*
*harerguṇāsvādavibhinnadhairyāḥ|*
*ārtasvarairvā ruruduḥ suduḥkhitā*
*advaitamukhyā dvijasajjanāstataḥ||1||*

*Word for word:* acharyaratnat — from the Acharyaratna; hi — indeed; nishamya — hearing; tat — that; vachah — account; hareh — of Hari; guna-asvada-vibhinna-dhairyah — their composure shattered by relishing (the tale of His) qualities; arta-svaraih — with cries of anguish; va — as it were; ruruduh — wept; su-duhkhitah — deeply grieved; advaita-mukhyah — headed by Advaita; dvija-sajjanah — the virtuous brahmanas; tatah — then.

**1.** Hearing this account from the Acharyaratna, the virtuous brahmanas headed by Advaita lost their composure as they relished the tale of Hari's virtues, and, deeply grieved, they wept aloud as if in pain.

**2.** And the Lord of the world, who dispels the distress of His devotees, resolved, "I shall go to the abode of Advaita Acharya."

**3.** Having wandered through the Radha country, He who is the one festival for the eyes of the people spoke sweetly to the great soul, the Avadhuta:

[^304-1]: Keshava is here a name of the Lord (Krishna Chaitanya).
[^304-2]: Pushpagrama ("Flower Village") — apparently Phuliya, a village near Shantipura.
[^304-3]: "Peerless" (advitiya, literally "without a second") — a play on the name Advaita ("Non-dual").
[^304-4]: At Badarikashrama in the Himalayas the god Narayana, in the form of a sage, performs austerities surrounded by the rishis.
[^304-5]: That is, food that is chewed, sucked, licked and drunk.
[^304-6]: Vasudeva Sarvabhauma, a learned brahmana of Navadvipa who lived in Puri; the meeting with him is described in the following sargas.
[^304-7]: The day of Hari is Ekadashi, the eleventh day of the lunar fortnight, kept with fasting and a night vigil.
[^304-8]: A blade of grass between the teeth is a sign of utter humility.
[^304-9]: Advaita wonders that he feels no pain of separation and asks whether it is the Lord who holds his love in check; the Lord replies that if it showed itself in full, He would be unable to leave.
[^304-10]: Gopinatha Acharya, a brahmana of Navadvipa who later met the Lord in Puri.
[^304-11]: In Haridasa Dasa's edition (witness C) this verse comes after the next one, which is more natural to the sense.

## Prakrama 3, Sarga 5. The Breaking of the Staff

*The Lord travels towards Purushottama with His companions, singing the names of Rama and Krishna; the toll-collectors; Nityananda breaks the Lord's sannyasa staff, and the Lord, feigning anger, admits that he has done His will*

### Verse 1

ततः प्रतस्थे भगवान्मुकुन्द-
गदाधराद्यैर्द्विजसज्जनैः प्रभुः।
पुरोऽवधूतं प्रणिधाय देवो
रराज काव्येन यथोडुपेशः॥१॥

*tataḥ pratasthe bhagavānmukunda-*
*gadādharādyairdvijasajjanaiḥ prabhuḥ|*
*puro'vadhūtaṁ praṇidhāya devo*
*rarāja kāvyena yathoḍupeśaḥ||1||*

*Word for word:* tatah — then; pratasthe — set out; bhagavan — Bhagavan; mukunda-gadadhara-adyaih — with Mukunda, Gadadhara and the rest; dvija-sajjanaih — virtuous brahmanas; prabhuh — the Lord; purah — in front; avadhutam — the Avadhuta; pranidhaya — placing; devah — the Lord; raraja — shone; kavyena — with Kavya (Venus); yatha — as; udu-peshah — the lord of the stars (the moon).

**1.** Then Bhagavan, the Lord, set out with Mukunda, Gadadhara and other virtuous brahmanas; placing the Avadhuta in front, the Lord shone like the moon, the lord of the stars, beside Kavya[^305-1].

### Verse 2

द्गतिः क्वचित्प्रेमविभिन्नधैर्यः॥२॥

*gacchankvacidgāyati kṛṣṇagītaṁ*
*kvacidvadedarthamalabdhasaṁjñam|*
*kvaciddrutaṁ yāti śanaiḥ kvacitskhala-*
*dgatiḥ kvacitpremavibhinnadhairyaḥ||2||*

*Word for word:* gachchhan — going; kvachit — at times; gayati — sings; krishna-gitam — a song of Krishna; kvachit — at times; vadet — utters; artham — a sense; alabdha-samjnam — that finds no name; kvachit — at times; drutam — quickly; yati — goes; shanaih — slowly; kvachit — at times; skhalat-gatih — with stumbling gait; kvachit — at times; prema-vibhinna-dhairyah — His composure shattered by love.

**2.** As He went, at times He sang a song of Krishna, at times He uttered something indistinct for which there were no words; at times He walked fast, at times slowly, at times stumbling, and at times His composure was shattered by love.

रात्रौ च गायत्यथ रौति धैर्यं
विसृज्य देवो महतां सुखाय॥३॥

*sāyaṁ kvacidbhakṣyamupasthitaṁ bhave-*
*ttadannamaśnāti hariryathāvidhi|*
*rātrau ca gāyatyatha rauti dhairyaṁ*
*visṛjya devo mahatāṁ sukhāya||3||*

*Word for word:* sayam — in the evening; kvachit — somewhere; bhakshyam — food; upasthitam — offered; bhavet — happens to be; tat — that; annam — food; ashnati — eats; harih — Hari; yatha-vidhi — according to rule; ratrau — at night; cha — and; gayati — sings; atha — and; rauti — cries out; dhairyam — restraint; visrijya — casting aside; devah — the Lord; mahatam — of the great souls; sukhaya — for the joy.

[^305-1]: Kavya is the planet Venus (Shukra). Nityananda, walking in front, is compared to Venus, the Lord to the moon.
[^305-2]: The narrator, Murari, is addressing Damodara (see Sarga 3.1).
[^305-3]: Literally "his weariness gone": on seeing the Lord and His companions, the toll-collector apparently gave up his greed of his own accord.
[^305-4]: Shaktis are divine energies, the consorts of the gods.
[^305-5]: That is, he has set free the gods confined in the staff.
[^305-6]: The Lord admits that by breaking the staff Nityananda has only carried out His own innermost wish.

## Prakrama 3, Sarga 6. Wandering in the Southern Country

*The Lord travels towards Purushottama: Tamolipta; Remuna, where Gopinatha lets His crown fall to Him; the river Vaitarani; Yajapura (Jajpur) with the Boar, Viraja, Nabhi-Gaya and countless lingas of Shiva*

### Verse 1

इत्युक्त्वा प्रययौ देवो हरिकीर्तनतत्परः।
पथस्था देवता दृष्ट्वा नत्वा स्तुत्वा यथाविधि॥१॥

*ityuktvā prayayau devo harikīrtanatatparaḥ|*
*pathasthā devatā dṛṣṭvā natvā stutvā yathāvidhi||1||*

*Word for word:* iti — thus; uktva — having spoken; prayayau — set out; devah — the Lord; hari-kirtana-tatparah — intent on chanting the name of Hari; patha-sthah — standing by the road; devatah — deities; drishtva — seeing; natva — bowing; stutva — praising; yatha-vidhi — as is proper.

**1.** So saying, the Lord set out again, wholly intent on chanting the name of Hari; whenever He saw images of the gods standing by the road, He bowed to them and offered praises, as is proper.

### Verse 2

तमोलिप्ते महापुण्ये हरेः क्षेत्रे जगद्गुरुः।
ब्रह्मकुण्डे कृतस्नानो ददर्श मधुसूदनम्॥२॥

*tamolipte mahāpuṇye hareḥ kṣetre jagadguruḥ|*
*brahmakuṇḍe kṛtasnāno dadarśa madhusūdanam||2||*

*Word for word:* tamolipte — at Tamolipta; maha-punye — most holy; hareh — of Hari; kshetre — in the sacred abode; jagat-guruh — the Guru of the world; brahma-kunde — in the Brahma-kunda; krita-snanah — having bathed; dadarsha — beheld; madhusudanam — Madhusudana.

**2.** At Tamolipta[^306-1], the most holy abode of Hari, the Guru of the world bathed in the Brahma-kunda and beheld Madhusudana.

### Verse 3

ततो जगाम भगवान्दिनैः कतिपयैः प्रभुः।
रेमुणायां महापुर्यां द्रष्टुं गोपालदेवकम्॥३॥

*tato jagāma bhagavāndinaiḥ katipayaiḥ prabhuḥ|*
*remuṇāyāṁ mahāpuryāṁ draṣṭuṁ gopāladevakam||3||*

*Word for word:* tatah — then; jagama — came; bhagavan — Bhagavan; dinaih — in days; katipayaih — a few; prabhuh — the Lord; remunayam — to Remuna; maha-puryam — the great town; drashtum — to see; gopala-devakam — the god Gopala.

**3.** Then, within a few days, Bhagavan, the Lord, came to the great town of Remuna to see the god Gopala —

### Verse 4

ब्राह्मणानुग्रहार्थाय तत्र गत्वा स्थितं हरिम्॥४॥

*vārāṇasyāmuddhavena sthāpitaṁ pūjitaṁ purā|*

**4.** that Hari who of old was installed and worshipped by Uddhava in Varanasi, and who, to show favour to a brahmana, went there and remained[^306-2].

### Verse 5

गोपीनाथमिति केचिदाहुस्तं करुणानिधिम्।

### Verse 7

*daṇḍavadbhuvi nipatya sureśaṁ*

**7.** Falling to the ground like a staff, He bowed to the Lord of the gods; His moon-face grew moist with compassion, and He, whose eyes are long like lotuses, danced with His own and sang kirtana.

### Verse 8

तत्क्षणान्मुररिपोः प्रतिमाया
मौलिलग्नमुकुटं च समाप।
तदवलोक्य करपद्मयुगेन
तद्दधार श्रीशचीसुत एषः॥८॥

*tatkṣaṇānmuraripoḥ pratimāyā*
*maulilagnamukuṭaṁ ca samāpa|*
*tadavalokya karapadmayugena*
*taddadhāra śrīśacīsuta eṣaḥ||8||*

*Word for word:* tat-kshanat — at that very moment; mura-ripoh — of the Enemy of Mura; pratimayah — of the image; mauli-lagna-mukutam — the crown fixed on the head; cha — and; samapa — reached (Him); tat — that; avalokya — seeing; kara-padma-yugena — with His two lotus hands; tat — it; dadhara — caught; shri-shachi-sutah — the son of Sri Shachi; eshah — He.

**8.** And at that very moment the crown fixed on the head of the image of the Enemy of Mura fell right to Him. Seeing this, the son of Sri Shachi caught it in His two lotus hands.

### Verse 9

तत्प्रसादमधिगत्य स्वमूर्ध्ना
सन्दधार च रराज च हृष्टः।
अद्भुतं तमवलोक्य सुरेशं
खे ननन्द नतकन्धरचित्तः॥९॥

*tatprasādamadhigatya svamūrdhnā*
*sandadhāra ca rarāja ca hṛṣṭaḥ|*
*adbhutaṁ tamavalokya sureśaṁ*
*khe nananda natakandharacittaḥ||9||*

*Word for word:* tat-prasadam — that grace; adhigatya — receiving; sva-murdhna — on His own head; sandadhara — placed; cha — and; raraja — shone; cha — and; hrishtah — joyful; adbhutam — wondrous; tam — that; avalokya — beholding; sura-isham — Lord of the gods; khe — in the inner space (of the heart); nananda — rejoiced; nata-kandhara-chittah — with bowed neck and heart.

**9.** Receiving that grace, He placed the crown on His own head and shone with joy; and, beholding the wondrous Lord of the gods, He rejoiced in the depths of His heart[^306-4], with bowed head and soul.

### Verse 10

तत्र नृत्यमकरोदतुलश्री-

वैष्णवैः सह दिनान्तरमन्तः
सायमेव विरराम महात्मा॥१०॥

*tatra nṛtyamakarodatulaśrī-*

*Word for word:* tatra — there; nrityam akarot — danced; atula-shrih — of peerless beauty; nyasinam — of sannyasis; varah — the best; sudhakara-kantih — radiant as the moon; vaishnavaih saha — with the Vaishnavas; dina-antaram antah — all through the day; sayam eva — only in the evening; virarama — stopped; maha-atma — the great soul.

**10.** And there He of peerless beauty, the best of sannyasis, radiant as the moon, danced with the Vaishnavas all through the day, and only in the evening did the great soul stop.

### Verse 11

तं विलोक्य मुदिता जनसङ्घा-

तत्र सोऽपि रजनीं प्रणिनाय
भक्ष्यमन्नमुपभोज्य मुनीशः॥११॥

*taṁ vilokya muditā janasaṅghā-*
*stuṣṭuvurmuhuramuṁ praśaśaṁsuḥ|*
*tatra so'pi rajanīṁ praṇināya*
*bhakṣyamannamupabhojya munīśaḥ||11||*

*Word for word:* tam — Him; vilokya — seeing; mudita — delighted; jana-sanghah — the crowds of people; tushtuvuh — hymned; muhuh — again and again; amum — Him; prashashamsuh — praised; tatra — there; sah — He; api — and; rajanim — the night; praninaya — spent; bhakshyam annam — food to eat; upabhojya — having partaken of; muni-ishah — the lord of sages.

**11.** Seeing Him, the crowds of people rejoiced and hymned and praised Him again and again. And the lord of sages, having partaken of the food offered, spent the night there.

### Verse 12

प्रातरम्बुजमुखः स जगाम
